#3174. Marchex (MCHX) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Bundled AI actions are driving bigger customer spend, and management outlined a $100 million target.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Marchex, Inc. (MCHX +7.69%) reported its return to positive GAAP net income and year-over-year revenue growth following the acquisition and integration of Archenia. Management indicated that the company is transitioning from providing conversational analytics to a model that bundles insights with AI-powered automated actions to drive measurable revenue outcomes for enterprise customers. The company established a long-term annual revenue objective of more than $100 million while maintaining an annualized adjusted EBITDA run rate exceeding $10 million through expense efficiency and organizational realignment.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the Marchex Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the conference over to Francis Feeney, Chief Operating Officer. Francis, please go ahead.

Francis Feeney: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Marchex's Business Update and Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call. Joining us today are Russ Horowitz, our Chairman of the Board; and Brian Nagle, our Chief Financial Officer. Before we get started, I would like to take this opportunity to remind you that our remarks today will include forward-looking statements, including references to our financial and operational performance, and actual results may differ materially from those contemplated by these forward-looking statements. Risks and uncertainties that could cause these results to differ materially are set forth in today's earnings press release and in our most recent annual or quarterly report filed with the SEC.

Any forward-looking statements that we make on this call are based on assumptions as of today, and we undertake no obligation to update these statements for subsequent events. During this call, we will present both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures. A reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures is included in today's earnings press release. The earnings press release is available on the Investor Relations section of our website. At this time, I want to turn the call over to Russ.

Russell Horowitz: Thank you, Frank, and thank you, everyone, for joining us today. Our third quarter results reflect meaningful progress in strengthening Marchex's financial performance. During the quarter, we delivered year-over-year revenue growth, positive GAAP net income and significant improvement in adjusted EBITDA. Since completing the acquisition of Archenia in July, our focus has been on bringing together the complementary technologies of both companies. Our combined solutions help customers use insights from consumer conversations to qualify leads, improve call handling and convert more inquiries into appointments and sales. We believe these capabilities create opportunities to expand our existing enterprise relationships and reach new customers and markets.

Our expanded offerings are also -- expanded offerings also broaden how we generate revenue, and we are seeing encouraging early commercial traction, including expanded relationships with existing customers and deployments of new AI-powered solutions. Let me share 2 examples of our progress with customers and products. One example is the expansion of our relationship with an existing advertising and media customer. Following a successful paid pilot, the customer commercially deployed our AI Voice Agent solution. The existing relationship represents approximately $400,000 in annualized revenue. We expect the new deployment to generate incremental revenue in the remainder of 2026 and add more than $200,000 to annualized revenue from this customer in 2027.

This deployment demonstrates our ability to cross-sell AI-powered solutions while helping customers capture qualified leads and sales opportunities that otherwise might be missed. As we disclosed in September, we've also added additional customers for our AI Voice Agent solution and have been discussing paid pilot programs with several large enterprises. The solution qualifies callers when sales representatives are unavailable, helping businesses capture opportunities they might otherwise miss. Since quarter end, Marchex received approval from a major automotive original equipment manufacturer, or OEM, to offer our Engage for Service solution through its dealer portal. This enables eligible dealers to use OEM co-op funding towards the solution.

The approval follows an early access deployment across 75 dealerships within a bundled offering where Engage for Service helped improve service operations and identify missed appointments and revenue opportunities. It creates an additional channel for expanding adoption across the OEM's dealer network. The solution also provides real-time alerts that flag missed appointment opportunities and customer frustration, helping dealership teams prioritize follow-up. These developments provide early evidence and validation of the opportunity to expand adoption of our solutions within existing customer relationships.

These examples and the other points of progress we're seeing across the business continue to reinforce our belief that 2027 will be an increasing growth year and that we have a tangible path to a more than $100 million revenue business as we execute. With our current operating efficiencies, in 2027, we also have the opportunity to increase adjusted EBITDA levels beyond third quarter's annualized run rate of more than $10 million. I'll now turn the call over to Brian to discuss our third quarter 2026 financial results and fourth quarter outlook.

Brian Nagle: Thank you, Russ. Before we review the results, I want to note that the financial results we're discussing today reflect both Marchex and Archenia on a combined basis for the current and all historical periods presented as required by GAAP. Our Form 10-Q quarterly report for the third quarter will provide additional information on this accounting treatment. Revenue for the quarter increased to $16 million compared to $15.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. The growth reflected favorable customer activity, upsell initiatives within our existing customer base and coordinated sales efforts following the acquisition of Archenia.

Net income for the quarter was $1.3 million, or $0.03 per diluted share, compared with a net loss of $1.3 million, or negative $0.03 per diluted share, in the prior year period. The improvement primarily reflects the benefits of our operational and organizational initiatives, which significantly reduced operating expenses. Gross margin was 51% compared with 54% a year ago, reflecting the impact of our revenue mix as well as costs associated with the paid pilots during the quarter.

Operating expenses, excluding cost of revenue, were $6.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $9.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting our expense efficiency initiatives and organization realignment, which have streamlined our operation and reduced our operating cost base. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $2.4 million compared with $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, as adjusted. The quarter also included approximately $0.2 million of reorganization and acquisition-related costs. Adjusted EBITDA before those costs was $2.6 million. We intend to build on the stronger financial foundation while making targeted investments to support growth and maintain disciplined expense management. We ended the quarter with $8.7 million in cash and cash equivalents. Now turning to our outlook.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Marchex currently expects revenue of $15 million or more and adjusted EBITDA in the range of $2.3 million to $2.5 million. The expected decrease in revenue from Q3 primarily reflects normal seasonal trends as the fourth quarter has typically seen lower call volumes and advertising -- advertiser budgets impacting both Marchex and Archenia. We do believe that, based on our current sales pipeline and cost efficiencies, there may be opportunities to offset or potentially outperform the typical seasonality depending on the timing and formalization of opportunities, which will also provide additional visibility on growth acceleration into 2027.

We plan to provide our first quarter 2027 financial outlook when we report fourth quarter and full year 2026 results, which is currently anticipated in early March of 2027. With that, I will hand the call back to Russ.

Russell Horowitz: Thank you, Brian. Before we open the call for questions, I'd like to discuss the appointment of Travis Fairchild as President of Marchex effective yesterday. Travis previously served as CEO of Archenia, and before that, spent 18 years at Marchex in strategy and development positions. His experience across both businesses positions him well to accelerate commercialization of our combined capabilities, deepen customer relationships and support our next phase of growth. I'd also like to note that Troy Hartless will continue to serve as Chief Revenue Officer, where he will remain focused on new and emerging opportunities and sales channels to support our increased growth ambitions.

As I noted before, our longer-term objective remains to build a business generating more than $100 million in annual revenue. We believe the combination of Marchex and Archenia expands our opportunities to grow organically through a broader offering and deeper customer relationships. Our priorities are clear: expand adoption of our combined solutions, convert successful pilots into broader deployments and translate customer results into sustainable revenue growth. We will support these efforts with targeted investments in sales and product development while maintaining disciplined expense management. We will measure our progress by the business outcomes we deliver for customers, the revenue growth those customers -- those outcomes generate and our ability to improve financial performance and shareholder value.

We've also expanded our Investor Relations program to increase engagement with institutional investors and analysts as we communicate our progress. I want to thank our employees for their expertise and commitment and our investors, partners and other stakeholders for their ongoing support. With that, I will hand the call back to the operator for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Mike Latimore with Northland Capital Markets.

Unknown Analyst: This is [ Vijay Devar ] for Mike Latimore. First question is about what's the pro forma organic growth implied in your 4Q guidance?

Russell Horowitz: Okay. Thank you for the question. The -- if you look at our guidance of $15 million or more on the revenue line, you need to go back to last year's Q4, which I believe was in the low $14 million. And so we're giving a range today. So we are implying year-over-year growth on both revenue and adjusted EBITDA given the trends of the business and the outlook of our pipeline and efficiency initiatives.

Unknown Analyst: Okay. Of the initial 1/3 of your top 100 clients that received product presentations, so how many have purchased a product?

Russell Horowitz: Yes. We -- if you go back to May, we talked about some early metrics where we had approached about 30 of our top 100 and seen a meaningful number adopt one or more products and expressed our belief that, that trend would continue. And that trend has continued. We're not quantifying it today. We do intend to share more details and success metrics as we go forward. But based on some of the deals that we're looking to close between now and the end of the year, that will help inform some of the metrics that we potentially will lay out as part of our early 2027 guidance.

Good question, and we look forward to sharing more detail around those as we go forward.

Unknown Analyst: Sure. Got it. And finally, what's the average incremental ARPU from upsells?

Russell Horowitz: I'm sorry, could you repeat that?

Unknown Analyst: What's the average incremental ARPU, ARPU from that upsell?

Russell Horowitz: Yes. We have not given an overall metric on average increased revenue. We have given some specific product and customer examples that when we launched the combined solutions that bundle insights, actions and outcomes versus analytics and insights only, we've seen numerous examples of revenue per customer increasing by 50% to 100% or more. We've laid out a number of those, and we continue to see that trend continue when we're successful with upsells. And obviously, we're feeling increasingly confident that we're going to continue to be able to extend that model.

And we believe that our biggest opportunity to drive growth and achieve that $100 million revenue goal is really about penetrating the existing customer base given how much more wallet share is available to us based on the expanded product capabilities. So we have shared some metrics, as we mentioned, examples of 50% to 100% revenue expansion on selective customers and that we think that's reflective of what we can see as we penetrate and broaden some of our sales efforts.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Ross Koller with Koller Capital.

Ross Koller: Congrats on the quarter and the progress. I have a few questions today. First, Russ, last quarter, you mentioned a significant number of 7-figure deals in the pipeline. Is that still the case? And if so, how should we think about the progression of those deals both through the pipeline and how they scale over time?

Russell Horowitz: Yes. That's a good question, and it's something we think a lot about. And as we noted last quarter, we believe we have a double-digit number of customers where the potential is for 7 figures or more of incremental revenue. Within that group, we believe many of them likely have the potential over time to incrementally deliver multimillions of dollars of revenue per year. So if we can make this happen, it's very meaningful and a significant needle mover. For us, this has been one of the big takeaways so far that we have this big potential revenue expansion on a per customer basis.

And we believe our expanded TAM just on existing customers is very significant, and it's why we're working with urgency on building the momentum. In terms of hitting on the question of kind of deal progression and how to think about the progression of these deals, since last quarter, a number of them have positively moved forward, and we believe that will continue to be the case with others as well. Our goal is obviously to formalize as many as possible, but there are a few specific deals that we're trying to get done by year's end to contribute to our visibility on increased growth in 2027 as we enter next year.

Ross Koller: Awesome. And Russ, what's driving the increased deal sizes? Are there certain products that are resonating particularly well with the existing base?

Russell Horowitz: Yes. What's driving the increased deal sizes and the increased number of these potential deals is our ability to move beyond selling just the analytics and the resulting insights and now our ability to bundle it with action and revenue-generating outcomes the insights inform. When we can show tangible positive impact to the revenue line based on our actions, the dollars customers can and are willing to pay us goes up significantly. Right now, there's 3 or 4 new products that we're bundling and selling based on this opportunity profile. As I noted in the past, when we sold insights only, we had very little influence or control on whether the customer actually followed through and took action on these.

But in the absence of action, they don't achieve the revenue and value impact that our insights highlight. Looking back, taking those actions isn't trivial. It can require making operational changes, needing to mobilize cross-departmental collaboration, and other coordination in what are large, complex companies. But it's different now. With AI, we have the ability to more easily bundle and connect our insights to AI-driven automated actions. When we can effectively take the needed action on behalf of the customer, the outcomes become tangibly achievable and measurable, which changes how much they can and are willing to pay us.

It's another kind of virtuous element of this whole thing is that our analytics are able to objectify the improved results by measuring the value impact of the outcomes we generate through things like increased bookings, appointment rates and revenue. Good question.

Ross Koller: Awesome. And then the $10 million EBITDA run rate looks great this quarter. But in the PR, you mentioned targeted investments back in the business to drive growth. Is there any way you can quantify the size of these investments? And how should we think about the operating leverage in the business as you invest to reaccelerate the growth towards the $100 million target?

Russell Horowitz: Yes. Look, we're feeling really good about the strategy, the opportunity, and we are of an intent, as we've noted, to make selective investments focused primarily on sales and product development that can drive increasing revenue growth. But based on our current outlook, it shouldn't have any substantial effect on our EBITDA profile. And looking at our executive and management teams with Travis now in the President's role and the rest of us executing within our roles as well, we're now largely built out. And on the customer and product side, we have the key data and expertise capabilities we need to evolve our product sets.

So as we increase revenue run rates and harvest some of the operating efficiencies we already have planned, we can make those investments in further growth and still scale up the EBITDA beyond the current $10 million plus of run rate, which will also drive increasing free cash flow. We're focused on all of those kind of core metrics as we execute.

Ross Koller: Awesome. And then lastly, Russ, can you talk about the IR strategy going forward and how you're going to go about increasing the awareness in the investor community?

Russell Horowitz: Definitely. Look, first and foremost, we believe the -- our stock is meaningfully undervalued. I mean, we spent the last 12 months architecting the evolved strategy and executing and integrating the acquisition. And now we want to tell the story. We're going to be attending conferences. We have a couple coming up in Q4 and trying to pick up more sell-side research coverage. We believe the company has a very attractive foundation with our having established the $10 million in annualized adjusted EBITDA and a potential path to more. This is the highest EBITDA levels we've seen in over a decade. And we believe that we're going to -- we are and will be an AI winner.

Other companies in our tangential markets are being acquired for huge multiples of revenue. We're currently trading at about 1x sales on an enterprise value basis and about 6x enterprise value on an adjusted EBITDA basis with a business with accelerating growth and profitability. We believe the gap between our stock and where our stock is trading and the intrinsic value should close over time with our successful execution and our telling the story, which we're going to be increasingly doing. We look forward -- we really look forward to doing that.

Operator: We have reached the end of the Q&A session. I will now turn the call back over to the management team for closing remarks.

Russell Horowitz: Yes. This is Russ. We just want to thank everybody again for the ongoing support, and we look forward to updating you as we make progress, including additional interim announcements as we achieve key elements as well. Thank you, everybody, and again, appreciate everything.

Operator: Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#3173. End of an era: Apple Support Community forums will permanently close on November 20

Users visiting the Apple Support Community tonight were greeted with a message informing them that the platform will permanently shut down on November 20. Here are the details.

If you have ever had a question or ran into a problem with an Apple product, chances are you have come across the Apple Support Community, the company’s official discussion forums where users from around the world help each other troubleshoot issues and share tips.

The platform has a history dating back to at least 1998, when it was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Since then, it was renamed Apple Discussions before relaunching as Apple Support Communities in April 2011, with a redesigned interface, personalized profiles, and a reputation system that rewarded users for helping others.

Tonight, however, users who tried to access the platform were greeted with the following message:

The AppleCare Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.

You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.

We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.

Right now, the portal still shows a “Sign in” button, though it leads only to an AppleConnect login page labeled “AC Communities Web – Internal,” suggesting that access is now restricted to Apple employees.

Interestingly, Apple’s message refers to the “AppleCare Support Community,” rather than the “Apple Support Community,” which is how the platform is officially branded.

Still, the forums are already in read-only mode, with users able to browse existing discussions, search for answers, and interact with posts through the “Me too” and voting buttons, but no longer submit new questions or replies.

At the time of writing, the most recent post was published just 57 minutes earlier, suggesting that Apple only recently disabled new submissions.

9to5Mac has reached out to Apple for comment and clarification on the scope of the shutdown, and we’ll update this story if we hear back.

#3172. Claude’s new Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending – read-only, of course

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Anthropic has released what appears to be its answer to ChatGPT Finances.

You can now share your financial information with Claude and ask the chatbot for insights on your spending.

Also: Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info

Personal Finance in Claude, which Anthropic announced Thursday, reviews your connected accounts through read-only access via Plaid. That security measure follows OpenAI’s equivalent feature, ChatGPT Finances, which launched in May. Here’s what to know.

Functionally, this feature appears similar to ChatGPT Finances: It lets you link as many bank and credit card accounts as you’d like to Claude via Plaid with read-only access. You can then ask Claude where you spent your money this month or whether you can afford to take a vacation in six months, for example.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents

According to Anthropic, the feature is a response to existing use patterns: the company’s April usage report found that financial advice was one of the main topics users ask Claude for help with.

“For the accounts you choose to connect (and only those), Claude sees the bank’s name, each account’s name, type, and last four digits, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions. When you chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train our models.”

The idea behind the feature is that you can ask follow-up questions and request more insights about spending habits, trends over time, and future goals based on what Claude finds, similar to any other Claude conversation. The tool will also generate tables and charts to visualize your financial information.

“You can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due, or a dashboard of the numbers you choose, and Claude builds it as an artifact you can keep adjusting and coming back to,” an Anthropic representative told ZDNET via email.

Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now

You can also expect an ad-free experience in the feature.

“Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer,” the company said in the announcement.

The company added that because Claude is using actual transaction data and not memory, the feature shouldn’t hallucinate.

“It can list the exact transactions behind any number so you can check its math,” Anthropic said via email. “Like any AI, it can make mistakes, so for anything important, we recommend confirming with your bank.”

Still, the difference — and for many, the appeal — here is the natural language interface. Other finance apps don’t necessarily have an easy, accessible chat function where users can shoot off quick questions like they would to a human financial planner. These assistants also present historical budget analysis in plain English, rather than requiring users to interpret dashboards themselves, which users may see as a perk.

Also: 5 ways to use AI when your budget is tight

On Reddit, many users find ChatGPT Finances to be accurate and reliable. One Reddit user said ChatGPT Finance seemed to have Mint or Monarch potential, but noted it was still “weaker” than those apps in some areas, such as historical syncing, high-quality dashboards, and generating full statement PDFs.

“ChatGPT has genuinely helped me make better financial decisions,” she wrote.

Anthropic noted that users shouldn’t look to Personal Finance for Claude as a total authority. “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust,” the company said in the announcement.

“We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it” — indicating a more integrated financial planning system within Claude may be on the way.

#3170. 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

I’ve been a dedicated Pixel user since the beginning, so I was naturally excited to get my hands on Google’s latest iteration, the Pixel 11 Pro XL. I’ve been impressed with it overall, but I noticed that, as Google has done before, the device isn’t set up perfectly out of the box.

Also: Pixel 11 is $200 off in this early Black Friday deal

After spending a few weeks with the device, I found that several features are either turned off by default or need optimizing to work in the best way possible.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

The camera was the biggest reason I first joined team Pixel back in 2016, so it’s one of the first places I looked on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. New this year is Camera Looks, a setting that changes how images will be processed before you take them. You can change a number of settings, including contrast, shadows, tint, sharpness, and warmth.

Also: A week with the Pixel 11 changed my mind about Gemini

I’ve always loved the camera on any Pixel I’ve had, but I’ll admit that images can look a little over-processed at times. If picture quality is important to you at all, it’s vital to set this feature right out of the box because it applies to every image you take from that point on. You can find Camera Look by opening the camera app, tapping the settings icon in the bottom-right corner, and making your changes.

Pixel’s “At a Glance” lock screen widgets are one of the most sneakily useful features, and you’re missing out if you’re not using them. These widgets are off by default, but when you enable them, you can see real-time information without unlocking your phone. You can see weather info, sports updates, flight information, rideshare and food delivery updates, fitness information, and more.

Also: These tech gifts topped our experts’ 2026 holiday wish lists

To use these widgets, long-press on an open space on your home screen. To customize your widgets, go to Settings > Wallpaper & style > More lock screen settings > Widgets on lock screen. To access your widgets, you just swipe left from your lock screen.

Out of the box, your Pixel 11’s display isn’t set to utilize its full capability. The Pixel 11 series comes with a fantastic low-temperature polycrystalline oxide (LTPO) display, but it’s slightly throttled in the name of battery life. You’ll notice the increased resolution most on text and in fine details. It won’t make a huge difference to your streaming or large display elements, though. If you read consistently, either articles or e-books, you’ll want to make the change.

To change this, head to Settings > Display > Screen Resolution. Bump the setting from “High resolution,” which is 1080 x 2404, to “Max resolution,” which is 1344 x 2992.

If you’re anything like me, your phone usually needs a quick charge some evenings. The Pixel 11 series introduced Extreme Charging Mode, which accelerates charging by pausing background activity and non-essential apps. Google says the mode should charge the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro to over 50% in 30 minutes, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL to 75% in 30 minutes. From my testing, that estimate was pretty accurate.

Also: After testing the Pixel 11, I feel fine about skipping the Pro models

There are a few caveats: this feature is only available when your phone is at or below 50% battery, and you do need to turn it on every time you use it. But after the first time you do it, it’s available in your quick settings. Head to Settings > Battery & charging > Extreme Charging to turn it on the first time.

If you have the newest Pixel, you might as well take advantage of one of its biggest selling points. I felt like this feature was gimmicky at first (and I’m still a little grumpy it replaced my beloved thermometer), but the more I use it, the more I like it. The multicolor LED on the phone’s rear camera bump can indicate who’s calling, serve as a status indicator for Gemini, and more — and it’s almost certain that more usability will arrive over time.

Where I found the most use was when I had my phone on silent. After assigning specific colors to contacts (you can do this from the contact information screen), I could easily see whether a call was worth picking up without reaching for my phone.

To make sure you’re getting the most out of your new device, head in and change your contact HiLight colors right away. It only takes a few seconds and makes deciding whether to answer a call a lot easier.

We’ve all accidentally swiped away an important notification or missed a notification in a sea of updates. The Pixel 11 offers two notification features to help you stay on top of things.

Notification History is a feature that logs every alert from the last 24 hours, including those you swipe away. This is off by default, meaning when you dismiss a notification, it’s gone forever. With this on, you get a searchable, chronological backup.

Also: Google’s big flagship is more Pro than ever

AI Notification Summaries, as the name implies, takes long multi-notification threads and stacked notifications and turns them into bullet points. This feature is powered by on-device Gemini Intelligence, and you can choose which apps to summarize.

You can find both of these under Settings > Notifications > Notification history & Notification Summaries.

#3169. Usio (USIO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Record ACH volume and a new Harris partnership drove margin expansion this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Usio, Inc. (USIO -5.21%) reported its third consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability and a record year-to-date adjusted EBITDA performance. Management stated that revenue increased across all four business lines for the first time in 2026, with consolidated gross margins expanding 110 basis points to 24.1%. The company attributed this performance to significant operating leverage, noting that selling, general, and administrative expenses grew only 2% compared to a 12% increase in top-line revenue. Executive leadership highlighted the commercial launch of Usio Ion and a new strategic partnership with Harris Computer as primary catalysts for growth expected to contribute to 2027 results.

Operator: Excuse me. This is a conference operator. Thank you for your patience. Call will begin in a few minutes, so please continue to wait as they allow others to join the call. Thank you. Should you need assistance, please signal a conference specialist by pressing the star key followed by 0. To withdraw your question, please press * then 2. Please note this event is being recorded. The earnings release, which we issued today after the market closed, is available on our website at usio.com under the Investor Relations tab. On this call with me today are Louis A. Hoch, our Chairman and CEO and Gregory Mark Carter, Executive Vice President of Payment Acceptance, Chief Revenue Officer. In addition, Jerry Uffner, Senior Vice President and Head of Card Issuing, will be available during the question-and-answer session.

Third quarter revenue rose 12% and gross profit grew 18%.

While adjusted EBITDA increased 222% to $1.2 million Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 5% from 1.7% a year ago. This growth is also reaching GAAP results. Operating income improved approximately $743,000 year-over-year, and we achieved our third consecutive quarter of positive GAAP net income. These are meaningful signs of improving profitability. Revenue increased across all 4 business lines for the first time this year, led by double digit growth in card and output solutions, card issuing returned to growth. Our diversified customer base provides resilience, No single customer represented more than 10% of consolidated revenue during the first 9 months of 2026. Revenue for the first 9 months increased 15%, supporting our full year revenue growth guidance of 14%-16%.

Processing activity also reached new highs. processed $2.7 billion of payments in Q3, up 25% while total transactions grew approximately 27%. Consolidated gross margins rose to 24.1% from 23% a year ago. An approximately 110 basis-point improvement. Output Solutions made a meaningful contribution as investments in production capacity automation are translating into higher-segment gross profit and margin. Interest revenue associated with customer balances totaled $358,000 compared with $343,000 a year ago. Louis will discuss how Usio Ion is expected to expand this opportunity over time. Our cost discipline is particularly visible below gross profit. Total SG&A cost, including stock-based compensation and depreciation, increased only $105,000 or 2% compared with 12% revenue growth. Core SG&A rose just 1%.

The first 9 months, total SG&A was $200,000 lower year-over-year, while GAAP operating income improved nearly $2 million to $881,000 This demonstrates operating leverage. On $2.6 million of incremental third quarter revenue, we generated $817,000 of additional adjusted EBITDA, an incremental conversion rate of about 32%. That rate can vary with mix and investment timing, but it shows the earnings potential of putting more volume across our existing infrastructure. For the first 9 months of 2026, adjusted EBITDA reached $3.1 million more than double the $1.5 million generated in the comparable 2025 period. Year to date adjusted EBITDA has already exceeded the amount generated in all of 2025, positioning us for a record full year result.

Importantly, this improvement in profitability is also reflected in our GAAP results. In the third quarter, we achieved a $632,000 year-over-year improvement in net income. Moving from a net loss of $415,000 last year to a positive net income of $217,000 this quarter. Even more significant through the first 9 months of 2026, we delivered a $1.6 million improvement in net income, swinging from a loss of $1 million last year to a profit of $620,000 this year. This marks our third consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability and reinforces that our revenue growth and operating leverage are translating into meaningful bottom line results.

Operating cash flow more than doubled to $3.3 million for the first 9 months of 2026, an increase of 133% despite the prior year period benefiting from nearly $1.5 million in employee retention credit collections. Over the first 3 quarters of the year, we invested $2.9 million in property and equipment and capitalized software development, both to expand our productive capacity as well as to advance ION. At September 30, cash and cash equivalents totaled $7.3 million, an increase of nearly $900,000 from June 30. With only $1.5 million in outstanding equipment debt, we continue to maintain a strong balance sheet and significant financial flexibility to support our growth initiatives.

Together, these results demonstrate profitable growth and a strong foundation for the opportunities ahead. Now I would like to turn the call over to Gregory Mark Carter.

Gregory Mark Carter: Thank you, Michael, and good afternoon, everyone. Card revenue rose 18% to a third quarter record of $8.7 million with transactions up 17% and processing dollars up 7%. PayFac revenue grew 29% and represented roughly 75% of card revenue. We also saw improved attrition in our legacy portfolio. Our established software partners continue onboarding merchants while existing merchants increase activity. Acquiring merchants grew >60% with a similar growth profile in processing merchants. As a reminder, a single software relationship can bring us a growing base of downstream merchants without separately acquiring each 1. This partner-led approach is also helping us develop larger more specialized opportunities.

For example, our successful implementation of the filtered spend program focused primarily on smaller bodegas is generating interest from other similar organizations. Our FSA payments acceptance solution lets merchants accept FSA cards across the full range of eligible SKUs whereas closed loop programs such as a Medicare Advantage cover only a limited set of eligible products. We are also expanding relationships with fintech partners that can integrate Usio's capabilities alongside their own technology. These relationships can create multiple routes to processing volume including opportunities to offer more than 1 of our payment products to the same partner. Seasonally active customer programs such as county tax payments, should support Q4 processing volumes like in previous years.

Throughout the third quarter, our sales and implementation teams focused on developing additional pipeline opportunities and advancing software integration opportunities that can generate recurring processing activity as they go live and scale. Looking toward 2027, we have a pipeline of potential fintech integrations including opportunities to support partners that need additional processing capacity or functionality. As these opportunities progress from development to implementation, and live activity that can broaden the base of revenue generated on our platform. UCL1 continues to assist with expansion with existing relationships. We recently added payment acceptance for a tax assessor that uses our print and mail services an example of cross selling that adds value and can improve retention.

Card remains on track for a strong full year supported by continued faith PayFac momentum, expansion within established software partnerships, and a pipeline of opportunities that will contribute in 2027 as implementations mature. Now I would like to turn the call over to our chief executive officer, Louis A. Hoch.

Louis A. Hoch: Thank you, Gregory. Our results demonstrate the operating leverage we have been working to build Gross profit is growing faster than revenue. While the cost of supporting that growth is increasing at a much slower pace. The result is improving GAAP operating income adjusted EBITDA margins and cash generation. All while we continue to invest in our platform. 2 catalysts stand out as we look to our next phase of growth. Usio Ion which can deepen our customer relationships and expand our service offering and our new relationship with Harris Computer, which creates another path into utility and government customers. Both represent growth opportunities on top of our existing organic growth over the long term.

Potentially starting as soon as next year. We introduced a live initial version of Usio Ion in the third quarter. It combines business account functionality with our corporate and expense management capabilities and is designed to integrate more closely with the broader Usio payment platform. The next important step is enabling customers to settle processing funds into ION accounts accessible through this ecosystem. Rather than transferring settlements to external bank accounts. Today we earn interest on certain customer balances held in the ordinary course of processing. We believe broader ION account adoption will allow us to retain more eligible customer balances and create additional interest revenue and opportunities for cross selling.

Based upon our internal assessment, we believe the opportunity to capture additional customer deposits could reach several hundred million dollars. Harris Computer has selected Usio as a preferred payment provider and print and mail capabilities for relevant utility and government software customers. This creates a potential distribution channel into a large and established base of institutions whose billing and payment needs align with our strengths. The opportunity is compelling because we can support both physical and electronic billing as well as accept payments through virtually all payment channels. At the same time, we recognize that utilities often have lengthy procurement, integration, and conversion cycles. We are focused on implementation milestones and converting partner introductions into live revenue producing customers.

In short, we see a clear distinction between the earnings improvement already visible in our financial statements and the opportunities we are building for the future. ACH and complementary services delivered a sixth consecutive quarter of record electronic check transaction activity. E check transactions increased 39%. ACH dollars processed grew 26% and return check transactions rose 44%. While the reported revenue in this category grew 9%. That difference reflects a broader revenue category tiered pricing for established customers and a product mix. Our NACHA third party sender certification further supports our position in complex payments. Card issuing returned to a positive year over year revenue growth of approximately 1% in the third quarter. following pressure on revenue earlier this year.

Card loads volumes increased 6% and purchase volumes increased 17% as compared to the prior year quarter. We also continue to build on our implementation base. 15 new clients were signed, 16 card programs launched during the quarter, and more than 20 implemented programs in various stages of scaling. Card issuing is focused on converting these launches into sustained purchase activity and revenue over the coming quarters. Our card issuing pipeline includes additional programs with a key fintech partner. Opportunities to expand volume with existing customers, and emerging relationship with a prominent regional bank in the issuing space. We are prioritizing these conversion of these into live, recurring activity.

With pace and magnitude of contributions remains dependent on execution and customer adoption. We continue to support government and education disbursements. Over the past 12 months, we have facilitated approximately $1.3 billion in school voucher disbursements across 37 states. Primarily through ACH. and 5 of these programs are set up for card issuing capabilities. We continue to evaluate additional opportunities to expand school voucher disbursements. Building on our existing relationships and proven capabilities in this market. In a separate higher education program, 1 university is live using our consumer choice technology for title 4 refunds. With another 23 universities in the pipeline.

Our consumer choice technology is designed to let students, benefit recipients, and other payees from multiple disbursement methods including ACH, real time payments, virtual and physical cards, physical checks, and other supported digital payment options. This flexibility allows an organization to work with a single platform while giving the ultimate recipient more options. Output solutions demonstrates how targeted-capacity investments can translate into improved economics. Q3 revenue grew 14% while gross margins significantly expanded. We mailed 5.8 million pieces, up 7% and delivered 25.5 million electronic documents up 28%. That combination of volume production improvements and pricing contributed to our overall improvement in operating leverage. During the quarter, output solutions added 4 cities and 2 utility customers.

We are also better positioned to serve larger clients because of our new ultra high speed printer which became operational in the second quarter. With its expanded capacity and improved throughput, we believe that we are better positioned to serve larger clients. The business already supports hundreds of utility customers which gives our Harris relationship a meaningful operational foundation. We remain financially positioned to pursue a wide range of growth opportunities. With $7.3 million in cash, limited equipment debt, and positive operating cash generation, we can selectively invest in products and partnerships.

To summarize, we are delivering double digit revenue growth translating that growth into improved profitability generating positive cash flow and investing in capabilities that position us for even greater opportunities ahead. As we look toward 2027, we are particularly excited about 2 significant growth catalysts. Usio Ion and our strategic partnership with Harris. ION represents an opportunity to expand our banking and settlement capabilities capture additional customer deposits and generate incremental 100%-margin interest revenue. Meanwhile, the Harris partnership opens the door to a substantial new market of utility and government customers. Where we believe our integrated payment processing and output solutions offerings provide a compelling value proposition.

Combined with organic growth in our existing business lines, we believe these opportunities position Usio to accelerate growth. Further expand margins, and generate meaningful long term value for our shareholders. We reiterate our 2026 revenue growth guidance of 14%-16% and expect record adjusted EBITDA for the year. I want to thank the Usio employees for their continued dedication and commitment to our growing business, strengthening our company and creating long term value for our shareholders.

This is the biggest sale I've ever seen from Orion — don't miss this opportunity to get a smart bed at a low price

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you've tried breathable bed sheets, oscillating fans and frozen pillows but you still wake up sweaty, I've found the solution. The Orion Sleep System, now with $600 off in Orion's Black Friday sale, is a smart cooling system that helps defeat night sweats by actively adjusting the temperature as you sleep.

One of the best smart beds you can buy online, this clever mattress cover is fitted with a series of (imperceptible) water tubes that cool or heat throughout the night. That means a sudden flush of cold if night sweats are coming on, or a gentle warming if things get too chilly.

This is just a cover, so you might need to buy a new bed to go with it — I recommend our best mattress guide for our top rated suggestions. But with $600 off in the Black Friday mattress sales, there has never been a better time to shop the Orion.

I've never seen a bigger price drop from Orion, as this massive $600 off sale takes a queen down to just $1,795 (was $2,395). That's an impressive price for a smart mattress cover with active temperature regulation, particularly as there are no hidden costs (a sleep tracking subscription is optional at $250/year). The extras are average for this type of sleep tech, with a 30-night trial and 2-year warranty.

When we review any mattress, temperature regulation is a key concern. It refers to how well a mattress can kick out excess heat so you don't wake up at 3 a.m. feeling uncomfortably sweaty.

Most of the best mattresses in a box achieve this through cooling materials. That is, copper-infused foams or phase change material (PCM).

The Orion takes a different approach. This smart mattress cover is fitted with a series of water tubes, which connect back to a control hub. During the night, the water flowing through those pipes either cools down or warms up, so you stay at just the right temperature.

And this sci-fi-esque sleep system is impressively effective. I purposely warmed myself up to see if the cooling kicked in (the only time you'll ever catch me doing nighttime jumping jacks) and was greeted by a flush of coolness. For hot flashes and night sweats, this is a dream.

Most of the time, however, the Orion delivers the kind of comfort you hardly notice. It's climbing into a bed that feels just right, sleeping through the night, and waking up feeling snug all the way down to your toes.

While the temperature regulation impressed me, I was less enthused by the Orion's sleep tracking. At $250 extra for a year's subscription, I think you can get better results for less with the Fitbit Air or Withings Sleep Analyzer. Or, for cooling and tracking, there's another solution...

I'm currently testing the Eight Sleep Pod 6, which uses water to cool and heat your mattress to just the right temperature. It's more expensive than the Orion — although you can save up to $200 in the pre-Black Friday sale and get a queen for $2,699 (was $2,899) — but the integrated sleep tracking is accurate and intuitive, delivering detailed insight into your rest. A subscription is required and starts from $17/month.

#3167. CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt

CoreWeave's credit stress continued to spiral on Thursday amid a broader sell-off in AI-related names.

CoreWeave — a so-called neocloud company — has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to finance its AI infrastructure build-out. It's now facing a rebellion from stock and bond investors as concerns mount about AI overspending and debt levels.

Yields on CoreWeave debt have continued to climb, with the yield to maturity on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reaching 15.78%. Bond yields move inversely to prices. Meanwhile, the spread on its five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, at one point soared above 1,140 basis points. It last stood at nearly 1,038 bps — a 16% week-over-week jump and 164% higher than a year ago.

Credit concerns are spreading into AI equities too. CoreWeave's stock dropped during trading Thursday before recovering and closing 5.94% higher. The moved followed Wednesday's 15.5% nosedive.

Other neocloud stocks were under similar pressure. Nebius also sank before climbing higher to close 1.29% and and Iren ultimately ended the day down less than 1%.

Anxiety about AI overspending is also spreading. For instance, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices sold off following a big sell-off in South Korean chip stocks. Micron closed up 1.87%, while AMD fell 1.5%.

While AI debt worries have been rising steadily, investors have suddenly grown skittish about the underlying finances of companies borrowing heavily to buy chips, build data centers, and rent out computing power.

Coreweave's credit default swaps are one place to see that stress.

Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. The spread widening in CoreWeave's CDS means investors view the debt as riskier.

The market is "basically saying 'no mas' to AI debt without operating cash flow support," the Evercore ISI trading desk said.

A spread level of 1,000 basis points or above is generally a sign of credit distress, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

No one is questioning whether demand for CoreWeave's services is real, since the company has contracts with all the big hyperscalers, Nolan said. The question is whether the cash flows will ultimately arrive.

"It's obviously heavily negative free cash flow at the moment, and it needs that cash flow to arrive really to justify all the capex that it's spending," Nolan said.

CEO Mike Intrator dismissed the market moves on Wednesday, according to a memo obtained by CNBC.

"When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," he wrote. "We are confident in our backlog which more than supports all of our debt obligations."

The backlog is over $100 billion, with around two-thirds of it with investment-grade counterparts including Microsoft, Meta, IBM and Caterpillar, Deutsche Bank said in a note Thursday. The firm reiterated its buy-rating on the stock Wednesday, calling the dislocation a buying opportunity.

"The problem is this kind of concern can prove to be a self-fulfilling prophecy, and risks triggering broader issues in other AI-related names," said Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research.

Domino effects may already be happening. Oracle's five-year CDS spread also spiked this week. It was last at 282 basis points, a roughly 10% increase in one week.

"A downgrade from its BBB rating would risk pressuring IG-only investors into forced sales," Reid said.

#3166. 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Most HR professionals say they believe employees can be reskilled for AI jobs, yet companies still often seek outside hires. Here's why.

HR leaders are confident that current employees can be trained for jobs created by artificial intelligence. Organizations are hiring externally instead.

That’s the finding in new research from Careerminds, a global provider of workforce solutions. The study, published in Careerminds’ white paper, The AI Redeployment Gap: What Companies Lose by Hiring over Reskilling, reveals that 92% of HR professionals and 88% of people managers believe employees within their organizations could be reskilled for AI-related roles.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Yet 51% of HR professionals and 47% of people managers report that their organizations are hiring externally for new AI-related positions, compared with just 42% in each group who report redeploying existing employees.

The research was conducted in partnership with Censuswide and surveyed 595 US HR professionals and 547 US people managers, ages 25–65, working at organizations with 500-10,000 or more employees. The research was conducted May 15–26, 2026.

Also: Businesses finally seeing AI ROI, but 62% can’t handle the storage demands

“Companies are investing in AI while potentially overlooking one of their most valuable resources: the people they already employ,” said Mark Saddic, senior partner at Careerminds, in a press release.

“Our research shows that organizations largely believe their employees can adapt to AI-driven change, but that confidence isn’t consistently translating into opportunities. Before looking outside the organization, leaders need to understand the skills they already have, identify where employees can grow, and establish a clear process for making those transitions possible.”

Reskilling, especially for AI, isn’t easy to track. Limited visibility into individual skill sets and which employees should be reskilled was cited as a potential barrier by 43% of HR professionals and 34% of managers.

Also: Pearson’s Workera deal targets a big workplace problem: No time to AI upskill

It’s not the first time that the management of skills development has come up regarding AI. In September, educational giant Pearson agreed to acquire Workera, the AI-native skills platform used by organizations such as ServiceNow, Accenture, and the US Space Force.

Careermind’s data revealed that 87% of HR pros and 84% of managers believe their organizations are adequately considering reskilling employees for future roles. However, the findings suggest that these organizations may believe they are prioritizing internal talent development, even though their hiring practices reveal otherwise.

Response to AI-related workforce needs isn’t equal across the board. The findings reveal significant differences in how industries are responding to these needs.

Also: Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

For example, in the technology and telecom industries, external hiring outpaces redeployment by 15%. At the same time, media and entertainment is the only sector surveyed in which both groups report redeployment at least as frequently as external hiring. Among HR professionals in that industry, 56% report redeploying employees, compared with just 25% who hire externally.

Separate research from The Josh Bersin Company, cited in the Careerminds white paper, reveals that external hiring can cost three to five times more than filling comparable roles internally — and on average takes up to 20 days longer.

#3165. Apple will monitor your public iCloud links now, starting with iOS 27.3

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Under Apple's new policy, the company will scan publicly shared iCloud links for harmful content - and possibly ban violators.

Be careful what you share in your iCloud. Apple announced it will start monitoring public iCloud links for harmful content — and potentially disable accounts that violate company policy.

Also: How to free up your iPhone storage almost immediately

The change comes with the impending release of Apple’s 27.3 build across its operating systems. If an iCloud user selects “Anyone with the link” when sharing something in a group chat or Discord server, it’s considered a public link; Apple is within its rights to scan for anything that violates company policy or is potentially illegal.

If you try to upload harmful content, Apple says it reserves the right to “move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete” your content at any time. Furthermore, Apple outlines possible actions it may take, including:

Apple’s announcement did not explain what “harmful content” would mean in practice. While there are obvious violations like drug sales and child sex abuse material, the new policy’s vagueness is concerning.

Once an iCloud link is shared under the “Anyone with a link” designation, end-to-end encryption is removed, even if either party has enabled Advanced Data Protection, which allows Apple to view the link’s content.

If you select “People you choose,” which limits access to users who have been invited or approved, the encryption remains in place, and Apple won’t be able to see what you’re sharing.

The new policy does not lay out an appeals process if you think your account or content has been falsely flagged as harmful. However, Apple does have a web page that provides information on how to appeal for other reasons. So there is a framework in place to push back if you think you’ve been caught in the dragnet by accident.

#3164. AI-Driven Tech Layoffs Could Trigger a 1.6 Million Job Recession

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With more than 200,000 job cuts in the tech industry in 2026, the bigger question is if layoffs will spread to retail and finance.

When Meta began laying off 8,000 people in May, it felt like an omen. Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, had seen several high-profile failures, from the death of the metaverse to its multibillion-dollar court setbacks. The Magnificent Seven — the tech giants that drive US stock market gains — seemed to hit a plateau over the last year, as more investors expressed concern about a potential AI bubble.

A wave of recent tech layoffs and buyouts reveals a growing volatility in the tech industry, as major companies restructure to cut costs and redirect spending toward AI. In just the last few weeks, Google extended its voluntary buyout program to select employees in five countries, and the graphic design platform Canva reduced its staff by 22%, laying off or relocating 1,271 employees.

Companies that have laid off or offered buyouts to 1,000 or more employees this year include Microsoft (60,000), Oracle (21,000), Amazon (17,000 in addition to 14,000 in 2025), Uber (3,300) and Netflix (1,000). According to the TrueUp tech layoffs tracker, layoffs are accelerating faster than last year, with over 200,000 workers reduced so far in 2026. The cuts aren’t limited to struggling companies, but are affecting profitable organizations with strong revenues.

The dominant factor behind layoffs has been AI. Companies have spent billions of dollars on the technology, plus a terrifying $3.2 trillion (with a “T”) that, Goldman Sachs says, doesn’t show up on balance sheets. With current returns failing to justify the massive scale of capital expenditure, companies are slashing labor costs and relying on AI to offset the resulting productivity losses.

While the US isn’t officially in a recession (yet), there are growing fears that mass layoffs could spread to other sectors, such as retailers and financial companies, creating a large wave of workforce reductions in the country. Analysts warn that if job losses extend beyond the tech industry, it could result in another 1.6 million people being laid off, bringing the formal unemployment rate closer to recession-level.

With several economic pressures at play — inflation, higher interest rates and rising energy and computing costs — buyouts and layoffs allow company executives to reduce operating expenses while investing heavily in AI infrastructure, automation and specialized technical talent. That hasn’t worked out in all cases. A handful of companies, including Salesforce and Ford, ended up rehiring or hiring new people after AI-driven layoffs.

Even companies currently reducing their workforce, such as Canva, appear to be offering friendly terms, potentially to avoid burning bridges. As part of its severance package, Canva gave outgoing employees $10,000 grants, MacBooks, six months of salary and a year of healthcare. For many workers without a union contract, that will be the best-case scenario if the economy goes south.

Canva’s terms for departing employees are both exceedingly generous and a window into modern tech:* Six months salary* A year healthcare* A year of LinkedIn premium* A $10k grant to start a business* Keep your MacBook https://t.co/Hqdegdb8Ek pic.twitter.com/pKuj8lJDvB

Job instability, stagnant wages and rising prices have been the norm for several years, arguably since the last major US recession in 2020, at the start of the pandemic. Given that recessions historically occur about every six years (regardless of which party is in the White House), a larger downturn could be on the horizon, especially if an AI market correction triggers further stock declines and widespread layoffs. If high-cost data centers lose clients and major IPOs falter, enterprises will likely slash spending and jobs as the promise of AI-driven efficiency fades.

So far, layoffs don’t appear to be spreading to other industries, and overall job cuts are the lowest since 2022. But the job market has become increasingly precarious, especially for younger workers, according to Lisa Countryman-Quiroz, CEO of JVS Bay Area, a workforce nonprofit.

For example, entry-level hires are down by a third in the most AI-exposed occupations since 2021, which could affect sectors like retail and finance —typical entry-level gateways for many young people. Household wages aren’t keeping up with expenses, and many job seekers have found themselves unemployed for more than six months. “While we may or may not see broadening layoffs, I’m concerned about the erosion of stable career pathways,” Countryman-Quiroz said. The one bright spot seems to be in healthcare, with 42,000 jobs added last month.

The 2026 midterm elections could also indirectly affect tech layoffs, mainly due to changes in the political and regulatory environment around AI and data centers. In the lead-up to the midterms, the backlash against data centers and tech billionaires became a pressing issue for candidates. Campaigns around data center moratoriums helped some Democratic candidates, including Gina Hinojosa, the surprise gubernatorial winner in Texas, where Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has his home and business headquarters.

Pausing new data center construction will be a shot in the arm for communities protesting the drain of AI infrastructure on local resources. But any slowdown in the buildout could also reduce demand for construction, chip suppliers or technical roles tied to AI expansion.

The midterm elections also affected financial markets, with technology and AI-linked stocks falling as investors worried that Democrats might impose new guardrails on AI. A weaker market can often make companies more cautious about hiring, capital spending and staffing, which could exacerbate cost-cutting pressures and lead to more layoffs and buyouts.

Countryman-Quiroz suggested that Congress could address AI’s disruption by investing in more job training, especially in growing areas like healthcare. “Current federal funding is only sufficient to train about 200,000 workers per year, a fraction of what’s needed,” she said. “Workforce development has historically enjoyed bipartisan support, so there is an opportunity for both parties to work together on solutions.”

I live in one of the most densely populated states in the country, but even with New Jersey’s small size, there are still dead zones lurking around. Google Fi is tackling this persistent problem in 2026 with the rollout of its new "super network," which is designed to automatically switch between two 5G cellular networks in real time.

Google Fi’s "super network" switching is powered by Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology, which essentially allows a single physical eSIM to run two carrier profiles at the same time. Instead of treating the second connection as an inactive backup, the phone maintains active links to two separate cellular 5G networks. Therefore, if the signal degrades — whether due to congestion, tower interference, or physical obstacles — Google Fi's software automatically switches over to the secondary connection to prevent dropouts. It directly tackles the dead zones that cause reels to buffer or download speeds to crater.

While Google’s announcement doesn’t explicitly name which carriers it's partnering with to pull this off — choosing instead to label them simply as "two of America's fastest 5G networks" — there are plenty of clues. T-Mobile remains Google Fi’s primary host carrier, while the secondary partner providing the dual-coverage failover is described in as a "major carrier," defined as an "MNO or MVNO with more than 1 million customers in the U.S. as of March 2025."

Even the strongest cellular signal can struggle inside crowded spaces like airport terminals, shopping malls, and dense high-rises. That’s where Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+ steps in to supplement coverage by automatically identifying and linking your phone to high-quality public Wi-Fi networks. It does this without requiring manual logins, portal verifications, or toggling Wi-Fi menus, keeping the handoff completely seamless.

Google Fi is carrying the super network abroad as well, enabling real-time network switching and Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+ across international travel destinations. By pairing dual-carrier 5G failover on the road with automated Wi-Fi in crowded venues, Google Fi makes staying reliably connected practically effortless no matter where you travel.

#3161. Ford Just Proved Its EV Battery Health Barely Degrades After 5 Years

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

2021 Mustang Mach-E electric SUVs have kept most of their battery and range after thousands of miles on the road.

Real-world battery life for phones, laptops and other electronic devices can diminish over years of use, but does the same happen to electric cars after thousands of miles and hundreds of recharges? According to data published by Ford this week: Yes, but not as badly as you might fear.

The automaker published a report analyzing the battery state of health of more than 36,000 Mustang Mach-E electric SUVs sold to customers across the US and Canada during the initial 2021 model year. After more than five years on the road — and an estimated 2 billion cumulative miles driven — the fleet averaged 92% battery health.

I call that impressive, but not totally surprising. That battery durability data is largely in line with what I’ve seen reported across the industry by other automakers and independent analysts.

One of the biggest concerns of early EV adopters a decade ago (also shared by fence-sitters today) is long-term reliability. The battery is by far the most expensive component of an electric car, and owners want to know their shiny new EV will last as long as the combustion car it replaces.

Battery longevity is particularly important as more used EVs enter the market. Many experts (myself included) have touted pre-owned and off-lease EV deals as a way to bypass the electric-car price premium, but shoppers may be hesitant to roll the dice on higher-mileage vehicles. Many fear a used EV won’t meet their range needs or, worse, could blindside them with an expensive battery replacement.

Ford’s study is another data point that could help allay those worries.

Ford examined more than 36,000 individual vehicles delivered to customers across all 50 US states and Canada during the EV’s first year of sales. A little more than five years later, the automaker says that around 95% of vehicles surveyed retained between 87% and 97% of their battery health (an average of 92%) across the entire 2021 fleet after an estimated 2 billion cumulative miles driven.

Better battery health means an EV keeps delivering more of its advertised range as the odometer climbs. The 2021 Mustang Mach-E rolled off the assembly line with an EPA-estimated range between 211 and 305 miles, depending on the spec, which means that owners lost around 16 to 24 miles of range over time, according to my back-of-the-napkin math.

That said, there’s no beating the chemistry. Around 2,000 vehicles in the group crossed the 100,000-mile mark, retaining around 91% health. A smaller subset of about 30 drivers reached 200,000 miles in their Mach-Es, with an average battery health of 88%. More miles, it seems, means more wear.

At the extreme anecdotal end of the spectrum, one owner put more than 400,000 miles on his original battery — though Ford didn’t state the specific health of that 2022 Mach-E.

An independent study published by Aviloo earlier this year adds credence to Ford’s reported numbers. An Austrian EV battery diagnostics firm analyzed over 500,000 EVs from 20 global brands to measure battery degradation — at 50,000, 100,000 and 150,000 kilometers — finding that many popular models maintained over 90% battery health at high mileage.

Tesla’s Model Y, which competes directly with the Mach-E, was found to hold around 90.3% battery health at 150,000 kilometers (93,205 miles). Aviloo reported that the Volkswagen ID4 and Hyundai Ioniq 5 showed 90.6% and 92.8% retention, respectively, over the same surveyed mileage. The first-generation Nissan Leaf — a much older EV with a smaller battery — showed more degradation at 86.3%, an unfortunate double whammy given its shorter initial range.

According to Ford’s engineers and battery chemists, the Mach-E’s battery was designed to last at least 10 years, adding that the 2021 models in the study use an older nickel-cobalt-manganese, or NCM, chemistry.

Ford’s new Universal Electric Vehicle platform, which will underpin the upcoming Fathom small electric pickup, will use a newer lithium iron phosphate chemistry. That will come with unique charging needs and different battery management calibration than its Class of 2021. The UEV architecture is also built around robust bidirectional charging, so we’ll have to check back in five or so years to see how using your car to power your home affects long-term battery health.

#3160. Thinking Machines’ new model takes the lead in western open-weight AI

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Another competitive model developed outside of China could change the open-weight landscape.

Thinking Machines Lab, a small AI startup from ex-OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, has released its latest model, Inkling 2 Small — and according to third-party tester Artificial Analysis, it’s set to give Chinese models a run for their lead. It’s technically proprietary until now, but Thinking Machines said it will release its weights next week.

Also: Open weights vs. closed: An AI civil war’s afoot

Chinese companies have led the pack on open models over the last few years. Models from DeepSeek and Moonshot regularly top leaderboards and rival the capabilities of much more expensive, closed models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Since DeepSeek’s R1 performed similarly to OpenAI’s o1 in January 2025, Chinese open models have given investors and high-paying enterprise customers reasons to rethink their expensive contracts with US-based labs. Western labs creating more competitive open models changes the landscape.

Thinking Machines’ latest model has 594 billion parameters and supports image inputs but outputs only text. The company noted its web and game design capabilities and that it evaluated the model’s approach to coding problems alongside the code it generated during testing.

“The result is a model that is both stronger at coding and easier to use inside real agent loops,” the company said.

Also: Nvidia takes another step forward for US open-weight AI

Inkling 2 Small scored a 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a composite test “for tracking progress toward artificial general intelligence” that combines benchmark scores spanning coding, science, and general categories. A score of 31 is above average for models in its class and is tied with Gemini 3.8 Flash. For context, Gemini 4 Carbon and Claude Opus 5.5 top the index at 60 and 59, respectively.

Thinking Machines said it will release the model’s weights next week, a practice that is becoming customary. Given the heightened security concerns around AI in general, AI companies spend a few weeks testing the to-be-open model with cybersecurity teams and safety reviewers before releasing the weights, rather than leading with the weights out of the gate.

French AI lab Mistral recently released its Le Chonk model via the same staggered process — it now keeps pace with OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Terra in coding abilities, which is rare for western-made open models.

Also: Mistral’s Le Chonk is now a top open model for coding

“[Thinking Machines’] plan to release its weights would make it the highest-scoring open weights model developed outside China based on current rankings,” Artificial Analysis said.

“Inkling 2 Small is amongst the leading models in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other models of similar price. It’s also notably slow per task and very verbose,” Artificial Analysis said. The organization also called Inkling 2 Small’s pricing “somewhat expensive” at $0.30 per one million input tokens, since the median cost for its class is $0.24.

Still, the model’s progress over its predecessor stands out to Artificial Analysis reviewers: Inkling 2 Small jumped 41% in automation capabilities and 20% in coding abilities. However, most models excel in certain areas or on specific benchmarks, making it hard to deem one or another the outright best coding model overall.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free

Inkling 2 Small also made some gains in accuracy, Artificial Analysis said.

“On AA-Omniscience v1.1, the hallucination rate falls from Inkling Small’s 61% to 27%, while accuracy rises from 32% to 34% and the attempt rate falls from 77% to 53%,” its review reported.
