#3093. Biotech stocks are surging. How investors can play the new drug innovation boom

Moderna gave investors a scare as its stock plunged on Thursday. But it's still one of the hottest biotechs this year. And it's hardly alone – the sector is on a roll and looks poised for more gains.

The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) is up 24% through October 23, building on a 28% gain in 2025. Two dozen of the ETF's 233 holdings have more than doubled year-to-date. Moderna leads the pack with a 587% surge — even after an 18% decline following a leak of clinical data for its cancer vaccine (which was actually positive).

Analysts say a new biotech cycle is underway, fueled by clinical trial results, M&A activity, and promising technologies such as genomics, mRNA — and AI.

"We're in the midst of a powerful innovation cycle," said John Hall, portfolio manager of the T. Rowe Price Biotechnology ETF. "What's super exciting is we're seeing newer modalities start to make it to market." Companies "understand the disease biology better," he adds, and that could ultimately lead to more novel drugs making it to market.

Investors are excited about technologies like mRNA and genomics, along with a steady stream of new drug approvals. The FDA approved about a dozen novel biologic drugs in 2025, out of 46 approvals in total. Roughly 66 novel drugs are in the pipeline for FDA approval, including potential blockbusters like Moderna and Merck's cancer drug for melanoma, and a next-generation obesity drug from Eli Lilly.

Analysts say AI could also lead to more approvals as companies deploy the software to speed up drug development.

"Biotech is a phenomenal application for artificial intelligence and machine learning," says Piper Sandler analyst Ted Tenthoff. "You can set up exciting predictive models that, frankly, can do things that we've never been able to do in the space in terms of novel drug discovery."

Granted, the industry is recovering from a fallow period. The sector's last strong performance was during the Covid era when ultra-low interest rates encouraged investment in early-stage drug developers, and mRNA vaccines fueled a revenue surge for companies like Moderna, Pfizer and Biontech.

The sector then went cold as many early-stage companies fizzled. Demand for Covid vaccines evaporated, and surging interest rates put a chill in IPOs and M&A.

The risks haven't evaporated – this is still a sector whose products take years to develop, resulting in far more failures than successes. But analysts say the outlook is healthier now. While that's reflected in strong performance and richer valuations, there's still good reason to invest.

Recent clinical trial results are stoking excitement that novel drugs in the works could tackle some of the toughest problems in medicine.

Moderna and Merck's melanoma drug, for instance, uses mRNA to trigger an immune response in patients, targeting tumors that have been surgically removed and genetically analyzed. It's not a preventive vaccine, but it uses a similar immunology mechanism and showed a 42% reduction in cancer recurrence or death (used in conjunction with Merck's cancer drug Keytruda).

While the Phase 3 results disappointed Wall Street, oncologists say the outcomes were still highly positive. And they see the technology as a potential game changer, ushering in an era of personalized treatments for cancers. Moderna and Merck have said they aim to submit the drug for FDA approval and get it launched in 2027.

Inflammation treatment is another promising area. AstraZeneca and Amgen recently released positive Phase 3 results for another use for their drug Tezspire, an injectable approved for nasal polyps and asthma. In clinical trials, it showed that it successfully relieved swallowing symptoms and healed microscopic and visual tissue damage in patients with severe throat inflammation.

Roche, meanwhile, notched a win after the FDA approved its drug Enspryng, a therapy to treat rare inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. It became the first and only at-home injection for adults with thyroid eye disease.

Obesity drugs are also advancing beyond the first generation of GLP-1s. Eli Lilly's retatrutide, a "triple agonist" targeting three different hormone receptors, cleared two more clinical trials over the summer. The drug produced 28%-30% weight loss at the highest doses in the study, Lilly said. The company plans to submit the drug for FDA approval in the first quarter of 2027.

Much of the innovation isn't just happening in drug-making – it's also in areas like gene sequencing, mRNA, and high-tech instruments.

Illumina has more than doubled this year. The DNA and gene sequencing company is seeing accelerating demand for its NovaSeq X high-end sequencing platform. Pharmaceutical companies including Bristol-Myers Squibb, Merck and Kura are working with Illumina to develop precision oncology solutions.

Another big winner is 10x Genomics, up more than 300%. The biotech firm offers its lab instruments to help scientists research cancer, immunology and neuroscience. The company's Atera platform is helping produce data sets to train AI models, a process that helps accelerate personalized therapies.

On the AI front, companies are using the technology for more efficient drug discovery, says Shreefāl Mehta, president of Guidant BioTherapeutics. Using AI, "you can now bring a drug to clinical trials with less capital. More investment is also going into companies that are demonstrating that," he said.

Global AI in drug discovery will grow from a $20 billion market in 2025 to more than $160 billion by 2035, according to forecasts by Towards Health, a research and consulting firm.

One other catalyst for the sector could be M&A. Dealmaking for biopharma hit $134 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $112 billion for all of 2025, notes Jeet Mukherjee, biotech analyst at BTIG. That's a positive signal, indicating more drugs in development are showing clinical promise.

It also helps that Big Pharma has a "patent cliff" ahead. Products representing $180 billion of revenue will lose exclusivity by 2030, according to research firm RTW Institute. Companies with looming expiries "are looking for novel products and innovative products to put into their pipeline," Mehta says.

GLP-1 blockbusters have also left some companies flush with cash for acquisitions. Eli Lilly alone has completed 10 acquisition deals in 2026 worth $25 billion.

ETFs can capture the investing theme, though they aren't all alike. The iShares Biotech ETF is one of the lower cost funds. It tracks a market-cap weighted index of biotech stocks, led by companies like Gilead Sciences, Amgen, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, and Moderna.

The State Street SPDR S&P Biotech ETF holds stocks in equal weight, offering more exposure to small- and mid-cap names. Its top holdings are Moderna, Natera, Twist Bioscience and Halozyme Therapeutics.

Piper Sandler calls Illumina and 10x Genomics the "primary infrastructure plays" in the life science arena, saying their technologies are "driving the next generation of precision medicine."

Piper analyst David Westenberg has a buy rating and $305 target on Illumina, implying 14% gains from recent prices around $267. He has a hold rating on 10X with an $80 target, above recent prices around $70.

Twist Bioscience is another name to consider. The company makes customized synthetic DNA and sells DNA sequencing tools. Twist has partnered with Eli Lilly's AI and machine-learning platform and linked up with Anthropic in August to start testing its AI model, Claude, for protein development.

Twist isn't expected to turn an EPS profit until 2029, according to consensus forecasts. But revenue is expected to go from $572 million in 2027 to $833 million in 2029. Analysts have an average target of $168 on the stock, implying 21% returns from recent prices around $138.

In the small-cap space, Piper Sandler's Tenthoff likes Monte Rosa Therapeutics, a pioneer in protein degradation that selectively destroys disease-causing proteins.

The firm has partnered with Novartis to develop a drug for inflammatory conditions and autoimmune diseases. The companies announced a Phase 2 clinical study in September for an autoimmune disease treatment, which has been "triggering milestones to Monte Rosa," Tenthoff said.

Tenthoff has a buy rating and $37 target on the stock, which recently traded around $10.70.

Also in the small-cap arena, BTIG's Mukherjee recommends Faeth Therapeutics.

The biotech is developing a novel two-drug regimen to treat breast cancer and other tumors. The regimen "has the potential to address safety and dosing limitations of another recently approved drug for breast cancer," he says. And it could become "a mainstay of the future breast cancer treatment paradigm and other cancers."

Faeth is a clinical-stage company that has yet to bring a drug to market. Yet the stock is up 93% year-to-date on positive clinical trial results, trading around $18. Mukherjee has a $55 target on it.

Kymera Therapeutics is worth considering too. The company is developing an oral version of the blockbuster drug Dupixent (made and co-developed by Regeneron Pharmaceuticals and Sanofi). Dupixent is an injectable, however, and oral agents "are frequently preferred by patients," Mukherjee says. "The drug has the potential to not only take share from patients taking Dupixent for numerous immunological diseases but also expanding the market to those not taking systemic biologic drugs," he tells CNBC.

Kymera has said it doesn't expect a patent fight over Dupixent because its drug is distinct, not a biosimilar or biologic copy.

T. Rowe's Hall also likes Kymera for its potential "to unlock disease targets that have been classically considered un-druggable." The stock is the second largest holding in T. Rowe's Biotech ETF, accounting for 4.2% of the portfolio.

#3092. Reddit’s New AI-Powered Reviews Are Already Controversial

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

The platform's test of automated product review summaries is sparking concern that advertising will replace human advice.

Reddit announced on Tuesday that it’s testing Reviews, an AI-powered shopping feature that aggregates user comments into product summaries, commerce links, and pros-and-cons breakdowns. In a blog post, the company said it wants to organically use discussions on the platform, from conversations about skin care treatments or coffee to headphones, to help people “understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them.”

The Reviews feature promises to make product research easier on a site that’s increasingly focused on shopping recommendations. But the announcement immediately rankled some Reddit users who are concerned it will degrade authentic human-to-human discussion and advice. Many Reddit moderators, or “mods,” tasked with keeping order of communities called subreddits, believe it’ll be hard to distinguish real opinions from straight-up advertising.

According to Reddit, the upcoming feature will surface product reviews in search results and through highlighted product mentions in comment threads, regardless of a group’s rules preventing the promotion of products by users or brands.

The test launch of Reviews, which was previewed in February and focused on electronics, will start with about 10,000 products across electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel. If the experiment works, Reddit plans to expand the feature outside the US and also increase the range of categories and products.

In a Reddit community for the moderators who enforce platform and subreddit rules, the new AI-powered shopping feature was greeted with skepticism and criticism. Writing in modnews, ProudnotLoud dubbed early tests “an ad-ridden, distracting mess” that made reading threads nearly impossible.

For moderators who work to keep commercial spam out of their subreddits, the feature poses an existential threat. User nerdshark warned that communities are already being actively targeted by stealth corporate campaigns, arguing that forcing Reviews into these spaces “does vulnerable communities a huge disservice,” especially without an opt-out mechanism.

Some Reddit admins have pushed back against the backlash, clarifying that the embedded product links are search shortcuts rather than paid placements. Yet users remain unconvinced. As CouncilofStrongs countered: “From a user experience, it is an ad.”

Reddit has also recently been testing advertising in search results, which could be a way for brands to reach Reddit users who click a product name even if they aren’t paying for placement in Reddit Reviews.

Given the amount of sites that focus heavily on human-centered reviews (you’re reading one of them), Reddit’s intent to aggregate product information through AI summaries could be seen as another way for traditional media publishers to have their content used without compensation.

But Reddit maintains the feature is purely informational. In a statement to CNET, a Reddit spokesperson said that Reviews relies exclusively on internal platform content and “does not source, scrape or republish third-party content.” The company said that because each review links to the original discussion, users on the platform “can explore the context and go deeper. “

Reddit also said that brands can’t buy ads to get into Reddit Reviews. “What appears in Reddit Reviews is shaped by Reddit communities, not paid placement,” the spokesperson said.

However, that reliance on organic Reddit activity brings its own vulnerabilities. One challenge Reddit may face with Reviews is trying to keep its AI focused on authentic human-written reviews versus posts that might come from marketers, coordinated astroturfing or AI-generated spam. Because the platform operates on anonymity, it’s facing an uphill battle with a massive influx of AI bots that could try to game content in Reviews.

The new feature comes alongside Reddit’s recent changes to the platform to detect spam or other manipulated content and keep bots out, including discontinuing support for RSS feeds and limiting access to its content API. The company is also restricting Old Reddit, a previous design version of the platform that has fewer ads.

A Reddit spokesperson told CNET that the platform has “the least amount of AI slop relative to other[s]” and that it is taking “numerous steps to prevent and enforce against inauthentic content.”

But while Reddit insists that Reviews will be centered on personal experience and uncorrupted by advertising dollars, many are worried the feature could blur the line between community research and automated e-commerce.

#3091. Bionano Genomics (BNGO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Flow cell sales hit a quarterly record as supply constraints kept back orders elevated.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Bionano Genomics, Inc. (BNGO +6.03%) reported financial performance for the third quarter of 2026, highlighting a strategic transition toward profitable growth through the routine clinical adoption of optical genome mapping. Management stated that the company is prioritizing high-volume users and menu expansion to drive recurring consumable revenue. The company is working toward achieving adjusted EBITDA neutrality by the end of 2027, supported by cost discipline and planned improvements in supply chain capacity. Developments in reimbursement, including a proposed Medicare coverage determination and new Category 1 CPT codes, were identified as primary drivers for future market penetration.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to Bionano Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions]. Please be advised that today's conference call is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Webb Campbell, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Webb Campbell: Thank you, Stephanie, and good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to Bionano's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. On the call with me today are Al Luderer, Chairman and Interim CEO of Bionano; and Mark Adamchak, Bionano's Chief Accounting Officer. After market closed today, Bionano issued a press release announcing its financial results for the third quarter 2026. A copy of the release can be found on the Investor Relations page of the company's website. Certain statements made during this conference call may be forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from such statements due to several risk factors and risks, some of which are identified in Bionano's press release and Bionano's reports filed with the SEC.

These forward-looking statements are based on information available to Bionano today, November 10, 2026, and the company assumes no obligation to update statements as circumstances change. During our call, we may refer to certain non-GAAP financial measures, which we believe provide useful information for investors. Reconciliations of these measures to GAAP can be found in our press release and slide deck. An audio recording and webcast replay for today's conference call will also be available online on the Investor Relations page of the company website. With that, I will turn the call over to Al.

Albert Luderer: Thank you, Webb, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to be here with you all today to share our third quarter 2026 results. Bionano delivered a strong third quarter. Our results reflect the trust our routine use customer base places on our products and the continued global utilization of optical genome mapping, or OGM, for discovering and analyzing diseases. Over the quarter, we saw momentum build across our business as well as the broader genomics community. Clinical adoption is what drives our results, and we saw progress on several fronts that make it easier for customers to bring OGM into routine practice.

We expect that adoption, along with greater use at both existing and new clinical sites to remain the foundation of our growth moving forward. We continue to pursue our mission of transforming pathology, the field devoted to understanding the causes, progression and impact of disease. Traditional methods for structural variant detection are costly, repetitive, labor-intensive and time-consuming. By helping customers move to digital workflows supported by our consolidated platforms, automation and decision intelligence software, we can provide a faster, more efficient and more informative way to analyze the genome. Today, I'll walk through how we have been advancing toward that goal across our 4 strategic pillars.

I'd like to take a moment to revisit the framework that guides how we execute. In September 2024, we made a deliberate shift away from aggressive installed base growth towards profitable growth with our existing routine users. By placing an emphasis on prospects most likely to become routine, high-volume users, we've positioned ourselves to be a more focused, agile and sustainable company. In practice, this is done through the following: first, to support and sustain our installed base of routine OGM and VIA software users; second, to increase OGM utilization by routine users by supporting menu expansion and improving ease of use with VIA and Ionic adoption.

Third, to build the support needed for OGM reimbursement and inclusion in medical society guidelines and recommendations. And fourth, to improve profitability and scalability through lower costs, higher volumes and continuous improvement in product quality. So turning to our first and second pillars, which are focused on supporting our installed base and driving greater utilization of our products. Q3 2026 flow cells sold were up 18% year-over-year at 9,870 units, a record for any quarter. In short, our customers are processing more samples than ever and a large share of that added volume comes from laboratories bringing OGM into routine use.

Now breaking down our revenue segments, Consumable revenue was $4.7 million in Q3 2026, up 24% year-over-year, driven by sales to existing customers in the Americas. Software revenue was $1.1 million in Q3 2026, down 31% year-over-year, reflecting a lower number of VIA software licenses sold in the period. Other revenue, which includes instruments and services, was $2.5 million in Q3 2026, up 24% year-over-year, led by higher instrument sales to new customers. The continued move towards more recurring consumable-driven revenue gives us a healthier and more predictable business and is evidence of our strategy in action. I'd also like to highlight the geographic profile of our quarter.

Revenues in Europe, the Middle East and Africa grew 14% year-over-year to $4.1 million, up from $3.6 million a year ago, driven by growth in instrument revenue. Revenue in the Americas grew 35% year-over-year to $3.8 million. Adoption of OGM is not happening in a vacuum. Its value is being recognized globally as the investments we have made in evidence generation begin to translate to adoption.

Regarding our second pillar, increasing OGM utilization by supporting software adoption and menu expansion, customers continue to give us very positive feedback on our software and compute upgrades that let them broaden their test menus and run more samples and in some cases, have allowed them to double weekly cancer sample throughput with no change to their hardware. Our VIA software remains the gold standard for CNV analysis on microarrays, and we continue to see adoption among NGS and long-read sequencing labs. Customers who use VA without OGM give us a base of software revenue, and this is often the first step towards using more of our platform.

Ionic, our system for producing high-purity DNA and RNA also remains a key focus, supporting both OGM and NGS workflows at scale. We are increasingly seeing our software offerings as an on-ramp to broader OGM platform adoption. As we begin to see the transition of array via customers to OGM, we will eventually recognize some decline in software revenue, but expect to offset this loss by bringing these customers deeper into our OGM ecosystem. As we focus our resources on the largest opportunities in clinical OGM, we view the migration of these customers to OGM as a critical step forward for more routine use. Now highlighting our third pillar, building support for OGM reimbursement and inclusion in medical society guidelines.

An important development this quarter was MolDX's proposed local coverage determination or LCD for OGM. In late August, MolDX published a proposed LCD that would set Medicare coverage in the Medicare administrator contractor jurisdictions that follow MolDX, representing 31 U.S. states. This coverage determination establishes a criteria for OGM-based genome-wide detection of copy number alterations and structural variants in hematologic neoplasms. The public comment period has now closed, and we look forward to the final determination. Today, Medicare is the largest payer for cancer care and about 60% of new cancer diagnoses are in Medicare eligible patients. MolDX states also represent roughly 61% of the U.S. population and private insurers often write their policies in line with Medicare coverage.

For laboratories, a clear coverage pathway lowers the financial risk of validating OGM and moving it into routine use, further supporting the broader adoption and utilization that drives demand for our products. This builds on the reimbursement foundation we described last quarter. As we previously noted, the AMA has approved 2 Category 1 CPT codes for OGM, one in hematologic malignancies and another for constitutional genetic disorders. Additionally, CMS has established reimbursement rates for both codes. The coverage determination from MolDX would add a clear path to Medicare coverage for OGM and hematologic malignancies. Together, we believe these developments are creating meaningful momentum for OGM and make it easier for customers to become routine users.

Another milestone this quarter came in New York, where 2 leading academic centers are now bringing OGM into their clinical laboratories. The New York State Department of Health approved OGM-based laboratory developed tests at University of Rochester Medicine, covering genetic disorders, reproductive disorders and hematologic malignancies. Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center then launched OGM-based hematologic malignancy testing following state approval. State approval is a significant step allowing institutions to offer OGM testing in New York. As more leading cancer centers adopt OGM in their clinical workflows, our base of routine users expands, subsequently driving utilization of our products.

Now expanding on our third pillar, the growing body of evidence continued this quarter with 3 new independent peer-reviewed publications showing the potential clinical value of OGM in high-risk myeloid cancers. The first published in modern pathology by researchers at MD Anderson used OGM to study 332 samples from subjects with myelodysplastic syndromes or MDS. OGM identified chromoanagenesis, a catastrophic single event genomic restructuring process in 15.9% of cases overall and 17.6% of newly diagnosed subjects. These subjects had a median survival of 9.9 months, while the median survival for the rest of this group was much higher as it had not been reached during the study.

Researchers noted that this information could help doctors identify high-risk patients earlier and consider more aggressive treatments. The second study published in the International Journal of Cancer by the University of Oulu, Finland, analyzed 48 samples of cytogenetically normal acute myeloid leukemias. The study found that OGM detected clinically relevant structural variants in 46% of cases classified as normal by conventional karyotyping and the presence of OGM detected abnormalities was associated with worse survival in these individuals. The third study published in NPJ Precision Oncology by the Josep Carreras Leukemia Research Institute in Spain, studied subjects with therapy-related myeloid neoplasms and younger onset MDS.

It found that OGM produced a result in every sample, including all 8 where conventional banding failed and identified 134 additional genomic alterations. OGM defined genomic groups showed significant differences in overall survival with chromoanagenesis emerging as the strongest independent predictor of inferior overall survival. These publications join the T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia study we highlighted last quarter, also published in modern Pathology and conducted by researchers at MD Anderson and Johns Hopkins. Together, these publications, along with the 365 studies published year-to-date, give us confidence that the expanding body of clinical evidence is a leading indicator of future adoption and utilization of OGM. Turning to our fourth pillar. We continue to make progress on profitability.

In 2023, our adjusted gross margin was in the low 20% range. Since then, we've steadily improved it. And in the third quarter, we generated a gross margin of 48% compared with 46% in the same quarter last year. We've applied the same discipline to our cost structure. Operating expenses decreased 12% year-over-year to $10.5 million and adjusted operating expenses decreased 9% to $8.8 million. As revenue grows and our mix shifts towards higher-margin consumables and software, we expect these trends to carry us towards an adjusted EBITDA neutrality by the end of 2027.

So I'll turn the call over right now to Mark Adamchak, our Chief Accounting Officer, to review our Q3 2026 financial highlights and discuss our expectations for Q4 and the full year of 2026. Mark?

The fact that we can effectively hedge the price of steel by inventorying a lot more steel than we need is secular. Now the fact that we have insourced a lot of our labor that is a secular advantage going forward. So again, I do not know how long this will last, but I would pause it not forever. #3089. Gaining Financial Control Requires More Than Just a High Income

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Income is one factor to feeling financially in control, but your approach to managing your money is crucial, too.

Earning more money can boost your feeling of financial control.

Nearly 9 in 10 (89%) Americans with a household income of $100k-plus say they feel in control of their day-to-day finances compared with 62% of Americans with a household income of less than $50k, according to NerdWallet’s October 2026 Financial Resilience Index survey conducted by The Harris Poll.

But getting a raise or a higher-paying job isn’t a surefire way to feel in control. Pairing your paycheck with good financial habits is a more robust approach.

Nearly 4 in 5 (78%) Americans feel in control of their day-to-day finances, according to the survey. That’s up from 73% in September.

There’s no single external measure for what makes someone feel in control of their finances. If you swap financial positions with someone else who feels in control, for example, there’s no guarantee you would feel the same way.

That said, a person who lives comfortably with what they have and who has the ability to withstand unexpected expenses has a good chance of feeling in control.

Americans with lower household incomes are much more likely to feel a lack of control in their day-to-day finances compared with those with higher household incomes.

That may seem intuitive. Someone with a high income is more likely to be able to cut back on luxuries, such as dining or vacations, when the costs of groceries and healthcare rise. Someone whose income is lower might not have expenses to cut.

However, that narrative is an overgeneralization.

If feeling in control of your finances depended entirely on having a high income, you might expect to see a much higher share of Americans with low incomes who feel they aren’t in control of their day-to-day finances.

But in fact, the majority (62%) of Americans with a household income of less than $50k do feel in control of their day-to-day finances. At the other end of the income spectrum, it’s clear that money doesn’t automatically result in feeling in control: About 1 in 10 Americans (11%) with a household income of $100k+ say they don’t feel this.

A high income alone won’t offset spending more than you earn, and it isn’t a substitute for an emergency fund. Good financial habits are an important component of financial control, too. They may look like:

Preparing for an emergency: Car repairs, medical bills, broken appliances: There are plenty of expensive emergencies that can pop up, even if you’re doing everything right. One-third (33%) of Americans don’t have enough cash on hand to cover an unexpected $1,000 expense if it popped up this month. Those who have an emergency fund can avoid relying on credit.

Managing debt: Monthly expenses that exceed income indicate a shaky financial footing — not great for developing a feeling of control. Nearly 2 in 5 Americans (38%) say they’ll have to rely on credit to manage expenses in October. Managing debt goes beyond paying your credit card bill each month. For example, if you get the maximum car loan or mortgage that lenders approve, a large portion of your paycheck is committed to debt payments. Keeping your overall debt load low gives you flexibility if your situation changes in the future.

Avoiding expensive mistakes: Saving money takes time. Spending it can happen quickly. A separate recent NerdWallet study found that 3 in 5 Americans (60%) say they’ve spent money on something expensive and later regretted it. Luxury items, gambling and vehicles topped the list of regrettable purchases. Pump the brakes on avoidable expensive purchases. For any big buy, take a day or two to mull over your options, especially if you have outstanding debt or if your emergency fund is low. Considering spending decisions carefully is another way to feel more in control.

The feeling of control is likely to emerge over time. Build momentum by making progress on one tangible financial goal — saving money or paying down debt, for example — before adding another.

Yes, Americans across a range of incomes report feeling in control financially. But it would be glib to suggest that this demonstrates that the feeling of financial control can be flicked on like a light switch, if only people tried harder.

There are plenty of reasons why the road to feeling in control can be arduous. Family obligations, medical concerns, affordability issues and limited opportunities can all present real obstacles, even for those who strive to practice sound financial habits along the way.

And Q3's been really busy in terms of standing that organization up.

The AUSA conference was incredible for us, just in terms of not just the amount of activity that was happening in Draganfly in general, but the specific buzz around AJ and a couple team members heading up Draganfly Defense USA, which would be headquartered out of Tampa. The other really important, there's a number, but the other really important thing to announce here is basically the Heavy Lift, we passed a 44807. The Heavy Lift, which can carry just under 67 or 70 pounds, now has clearance to fly BVLOS over highways and people. There's only about four or five of these 44807s that have been passed in the States.

One of the things that's really important about this 44807, not the fact that it's just done on such a big drone, but that 44807 now actually also applies down onto our customers. As our customers are buying this product, the waiver and the clearance is actually held by us. They still have to have their requisite licensing and stuff as well, but they don't have to go get a 44807 license as well. We hold that, and that stands for the drone, and then our customers actually get to use it. Really excited that we It's a lot more than just the equipment certification.

It's process, it's people, it's a whole stream of matters that have to be approved and pushed through by the FAA or approved by the FAA. Congratulations to the team on that. It has very big implications for sales coming up, as it relates somewhat on the commercial side, because as we know, these are used to stand up cell towers in emergency situations where cell towers come down. Pretty excited about that.

Also, up in Canada, the Defence Drone Initiative, which is Canada's CAD 2 billion+, actually, I believe it's CAD 3.8 billion over the next five years on category one, category two, and some category three drones, called Canada's Defence Drone Initiative, sorry, DDI. Within that, there's also a thing called the RFSA. That's the request for supply arrangement. This is something that's the equivalent of Canada's marketplace in order to participate in the basically the defense industry working with the Canadian government. Draganfly has qualified in the RFSA under all five categories, a big part of which obviously is the Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace.

You have to be a Canadian company to actually participate in that, and which basically lines us up, if we continue to be successful with what's happened here over the last quarter, and is indicative of what's coming in the future, then we should see ourselves hopefully getting a pretty big chunk of that spend. Just before I get to turn this over to the financials, we have seen our first down quarter in a long time. Now, we're very conscious of it. We absolutely knew it was going to happen.

We needed to do this in order to basically hold production capability for this current order that we're starting to work on now from the CAF, as well as a number of other not yet announced, not just initiatives, but situations or scenarios that we have to be ready for. I can tell you unequivocally that we have never been busier. We have never seen volumes moving faster. This is really a circumstantial situation that we had to account for, and we are pretty excited about what will start happening now over the next couple quarters to come, in particular, starting in Q1. On that note, I am going to turn it over to Paul Sun. Paul?

Paul Sun: Great. Thanks, Cameron. Thanks, everyone, for joining. Thanks for setting the stage there. Revenue for the third quarter was down slightly 5% to CAD 2 million from CAD 2.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. That was actually primarily due to some lower services work. Third quarter revenue comprised of CAD 1.6 million from product sales, which was pretty much flat year-over-year, with CAD 436,000 coming from drone services. Gross profit, CAD 129,000 compared to CAD 421,000 in Q3 of last year. Q3 did have a one-time non-cash write-down of inventory of CAD 367,000.

Otherwise, it would have been CAD 496,000 compared to the same period last year, where there was a one-time inventory write-down of CAD 43,000, making the adjusted gross profit of CAD 464,000. The adjusted gross margin for Q3 was actually 24.2% compared to last year's adjusted number of 21.5%. There was an improvement year-over-year from a gross margin and profit perspective year-over-year due to products and services mix comparing the two quarters. Total comprehensive loss for the quarter, CAD 13 million compared to a loss of CAD 5.4 million in the same period last year. This quarter includes non-cash changes comprised of a fair value of derivative liability.

This quarter only CAD 57,000, and that one-time inventory write-down of CAD 367,000 that I just mentioned. Breaking that out, the loss would have otherwise been CAD 12.6 million versus an adjusted loss of CAD 3.6 million in the same quarter of 2025. The increase in loss is primarily due to higher office and miscellaneous costs, some share-based compensation, professional fees, wages, and travel, and whatnot. As Cameron mentioned, we have been very busy in scaling the business from the same time last year. If we move to the next slide, we just kind of went over the year-over-year changes. So now, I will just go through the quarter-over-quarter changes between Q3 of 2026 and Q2 of 2026.

Q3 revenue decreased about 23% to CAD 2 million compared to CAD 2.6 million for Q2, mainly due to lower services sales again. You will recall Q2 was our best quarter, so we just had this timing as well as some services changes quarter-over-quarter. Gross margin percentage for Q3 was 6.3% compared to 20% in Q2 of this year. However, again, if we back out that one-time inventory write-down that I mentioned before, gross margin again for Q3 was 24.2% compared to an adjusted 21.6% in Q2. Again, the improvement quarter-over-quarter in gross margin was due to product mix between the two quarters.

Total comprehensive loss for Q3 was CAD 13 million again, compared to a comprehensive loss of CAD 11.8 million for Q2 of 2026. We had that fair value of derivative liability of CAD 57,000, the write-down of inventory. If we break that out, comprehensive loss on an adjusted basis is CAD 12.6 million compared to CAD 11.8 million, excluding all the non-cash adjustments for Q2 of this year. The slight increase in quarter-over-quarter is primarily due to some higher office and miscellaneous costs and wages as we have added more headcount quarter-over-quarter. Next slide, Cameron. I think we got the balance sheet.

Here you can see total assets increased from CAD 101 million to CAD 158 million, which is largely due to the increase in cash. The working capital surplus as at the end of the quarter was CAD 144 million versus CAD 95 million from the end of 2025. Shareholders' equity was CAD 151 million at quarter end compared to CAD 96.6 million at the end of last year. However, both working capital and shareholders' equity would have been even higher if we X'd out the non-cash fair value of derivative liability of CAD 376,000 for this quarter as well as at the end of the year.

We do continue to have minimal debt, and our cash balance at the end of the quarter was CAD 128 million compared to CAD 90.2 million, as we did a financing earlier in the year in February, as well as the most recent strategic financing that Cameron mentioned towards the end of September. With that, I will pass it back to you, Cameron.

Cameron Chell: Excellent. What I will do now is I am going to go to the Q&A. Just a quick reminder on everybody that this is our full product lineup. There are a number of other products that are coming out, being announced in the next couple of quarters as a result of some very direct sales processes that we have gone through with a number of different militaries. As it stands right now, we have got the Flex, the Apex, the Commander, and the Heavy Lift, which covers everything from something this small that is a strike, all the way up to something that can be carrying 67 pounds over distance.

We also have an Outrider version of that Heavy Lift, which has two diesel engines on it, which gives it up to seven hours of operations and up to 100 pounds of capacity. Then, of course, we have got the Orca, which has been just trailblazing like crazy as of late throughout a number of different militaries. Excited to answer a couple questions on that. We have got the SOTEN, which is kind of like our DJI Mavic type of replacement drone. Pretty excited about that product lineup as well as what is coming down and all the variants of these as well.

What I am going to do is I am going to just go to a bunch of questions that were sent in. Just let me get them pulled up here for one sec. The first one that Rolly sent over that came in is, "Revenue growth is still slow. When do we expect to see a real inflection point?" I would have liked to hope to see it would have happened already. However, knowing what we know about the industry now, I can see why that inflection point, it may be specifically for us, but maybe for a bunch of others, also hasn't happened up until this point.

I think we're looking to see that happen in a kind of like a Q2-ish of 2027, in particular a Q3. Frankly, that's about a year behind of what I thought it would be. What we're now seeing is that, well, in the U.S., it's probably backed off a bit just because of everything from the continuing resolutions and a bunch of election stuff and a bunch of money getting unlocked in order to flow through particular programs that us and many others have won. In other situations like Canada and maybe a few other militaries that we're fortunate enough to deal with, they're actually now just coming to fruition.

We did see our first win this year, which was the first contract that the Canadian Armed Forces let out under its Defence Drone Initiative, which is a CAD 25 million contract, so we're super excited to be executing on it. Excuse me. We have been very busy and expect announcements before the end of the year, at least on two more. There are actually 19 RFPs that we are involved with across the Canadian military right now, just to give you a size and scope. Those all took, they've all taken until this point to get there. We have been incredibly busy just keeping up with that.

Between that and some work internationally that will come to light here very, very quickly for the rest of our shareholders over the coming weeks, it'll be clear to see why we've not pushed forward with jamming a bunch of sales through that are sitting there ready to go now on production. We've had to switch some of the production lines because of some matters that have to do with sales and contracts being one. I think the real specific reasons of that will come to light here over the next couple of weeks for you. Canada announced a big commitment to drones in the recent budget, and how much of that do we expect to get?

We're going to have to continue to earn our way with that, but we do expect to earn a very significant portion of that. We have been scaling the organization in Canada, not just from a capacity standpoint, but also from a capability standpoint. We've made several key hires over the last six months in order to meet this demand that's now upon us, just in order to even to respond to the demand that we've had from bids and such has been overwhelming, much less now starting to deliver on it. As a percentage or how much of it, we're not really focused on that.

We are focused on doing the best job that we can and winning the business that we can do to do the best job for those operators out there. It's certainly over the course of the next couple years, well into the of CAD 100 million. Why did we invest in a Ukraine software company, and what is our strategy in the Ukraine? We invested in DoD Solution for a couple of reasons. One, they're really, really good at what they do, and they actually can supplement our engineering and software capabilities. They have a fantastic terminal guidance system. They are also part hardware and part software.

They aren't just developing software, but they've actually got the hardware that goes along with it. In the FPV market, there's one in particular kind of like dominant camera and board that's analog. Analog's super important because it's harder to jam. The latency is also such that it takes a pretty What's the best way to put it? It's tricky. You need to use an analog camera 90% of the time in your FPV right now. There is some stuff coming that will change that, but there's kind of like one dominant player that provides that out there. That dominant player is also an FPV provider.

The market is looking for a way to move off of their particular camera and board solution. Anyway, DoD Solution provides us that opportunity to do it. They also are supplying five other of the top Ukrainian, five top Ukrainian manufacturers with variants of their boards and terminal guidance and such. Just in terms of our network that exists in Ukraine and our ability to continue to expand that network, develop great product, develop great people, relationships, et cetera, we just felt that this was pretty strategic.

As mentioned, Kevin and I and a number of people are going to be in country in the next couple of weeks, and probably some more of this will come to light at that time. With the recent sell-off in most drone stocks, do we see a consolidation in the industry? Yeah, for sure. We've got a number of acquisitions that we're looking at. As you know, we're sitting on a pretty healthy balance sheet right now. We're very conservative with our cash. We definitely, as we move into this phase of the industry where there will likely be consolidation, we definitely want to be one of those companies that can afford to be taking advantage of that.

I don't know that we'll see it at the kind of like the top public company names for some time, or maybe if ever. Certainly for the next little while, I don't see it there. A lot of the private companies, a lot of the component makers a lot of the folks that were participating in the picks and shovels of the industry. I do see that now starting to consolidate into the known names out there. I know there's been a call for bigger consolidation happening, and some of that will happen, but I don't see it as prevalent as maybe what some others are predicting.

With the recent midterm election results, do we expect that to negatively affect U.S. drone-specific spending? Well, the budget went up to $1.5 trillion. Now it's going to come down to $1 trillion. That's still hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars more than it was before. So on the overall picture, if we were looking year-over-year, the answer would be no, I do not see an effect. If we look at maybe short term, I do see some squeeze happening in terms of more funds not getting released, things getting drawn out more, revenue being pushed out more quarters, just in general in the industry.

I do not think that is necessarily going to be the case for us now. I think we have faced most of that getting to where we are at today, as evidenced by this quarter. But I do think industry-wise, that is a bit of what will happen. However, overall, stocks need to be replenished. There is a rearmament going of an entire category of military strategy, tactics, weapons, mass low cost, mass precision. The cat is out of the bag. All of that is going to have to continue to happen. Historically, we have not seen Democrats spend less money on defense overall than the Republicans. I think in the big picture, the answer is no.

Is there going to be some short-term pain and some news media around how things are getting cut back or maybe that. Yeah, possibly, for sure. But every nation in the world right now is rearming, right, and retooling. So, we have got a 10-year policy cycle here of increased budgets. So, next question I have is, I have not seen contracts being announced for Orca. Do we expect any to come? Absolutely. Yeah, the product itself has been an incredible addition to the product line. It has opened up an entire new set of doors for us.

It has also given great capability to our existing product line, because remember, most buying is happening not for a single purpose, but for missions now. Being able to combine fixed-wing capability, long-range strike, long-range loiter, or long-time loiter capabilities along with the multi-rotor line has been fantastic. So the answer is, I cannot say more than that, but the answer is yeah, super excited what was happening there, and I think you will be pleased over the next couple of quarters. Are we still focused on counter-drone technology? For sure. So we were awarded a DEVCOM contract to develop a mobile counter-drone capability. That thing is moving along quite nicely.

There are already demonstrations happening in various different aspects of the DOW. We are continuing to push forward and invest in that particular area. We have been participating in bids and opportunities around counter-drone, in particular on our public safety, around security and private security. We really believe we built up a very significant pipeline of work in that regard, as well as what we are doing in public safety and on the military side. So counter-drones, it is just becoming part of what a drone company is. It is pretty tough to be doing drones at all unless you are also doing counter-drone.

So they are being one and the same has given us great advantage, and it is a lot of the same expertise, a lot of the same equipment, a lot of the same policy, so not a huge amount of cost to making sure that you can offer 100% solution to your customer. Then, final question here is, what is management's long-term and mid-term plan to achieve self-sustaining cash flow without relying on continued share dilution? Well, we are going to be driving three areas. So maybe just to recap. We have three particular verticals that we focus on. We have our commercial industrial, which historically was quite prevalent for us. Now it is our smallest division, but really important.

We do a specific type of work in there that is key, especially for the future. We have our public safety business, and we have our military business. Currently, the military business is driving things forward. We have Canadian military, we have U.S. military, and we have international military, much of which we will be talking quite a bit about over the next couple of weeks. It is really about just building size, volume in those areas now. We have developed incredible, I believe anyway, incredible capabilities in those areas that match what those particular militaries are looking for, and it has taken them those years, those militaries, to understand what it is that they really need.

We will be providing products into them, but also providing manufacturing capability. More of that to come in the coming weeks. On the public safety side, we are dealing primarily in Canada and the United States. We are just about to launch our DFR product, which we are excited about. Our campus facility, our campus program in particular, has really taken off for us. We are engaged only with three campuses right now by design, very simply because we are really working through all the very finite details of operations and training and such. We literally have a list of 1,500 campuses that have inquired right now. There are 3,000 in the United States in total.

We will go full bore on that after the next quarter, and we get through the rest of the implementation of these three so that we have got showcases, testimonies, use case scenarios, studies, and every question that can be answered around that. Also in public safety, we tend to focus on small, rural, tribal, sheriff, and border, because our equipment is really designed a bit more for heavier use, a longer range, heavier payloads, multi-payloads, things like that. It lends itself more to those types of environments, as opposed to being necessarily in New York or San Francisco or such, where we have got great competitors like Skydio and BRINC that are battling it out for market share there.

Then obviously on the military side, we are going to grow with the military budgets as they grow over the next number of years. Now listen, we also think we have got a terrific lineup of products that are differentiated, and we will continue to hone in and make those differences, continue to use our ITS team, our Integrated Tactical Solutions team, to embed with our customers and learn what is the things that they need the most, what are the nuances that make our equipment better use for them, and we will just continue to do more of the same.

On that, it takes a lot when you are building a company that has seven product lines to serve that type of a customer base. You kind of have to go wide first before you go deep. Now, that is against conventional startup wisdom. We're in a unique situation where we're a 27-year-old startup. We had the ability to go wide before we went deep, and so that breadth now is pretty much put in place. I think what you'll see actually over the very short order here, but certainly over the coming quarters, you'll see the depth of that now be able to penetrate and start to drive some pretty significant announcements and orders for us.

On that note, I think I've covered off everything. I appreciate everybody's patience. I really wanted to thank three particular groups. First of all, the people that work with us, our employees, the amount of commitment that we see in this organization, what people are willing to do to live our purpose, which is to be of service to others, and to save time, money, and lives. First of all, thank you to you. Thanks also to our customers, for sure, for the amount of feedback and input that you've been giving us, how deeply you're working with us, and how you have a long-term view of what your business can become because of what we can bring to you.

It inspires us. Obviously to our shareholders, thanks for your patience. This has taken a lot longer than we all thought. It has for the entire industry, but we couldn't be where we are at today without you. Man, we are excited about where we're at and what we'll see coming out in the very, very near future here. From all of us to all you, we really appreciate it, and we'll continue to do our best to be of service. Thanks very much, and talk to you soon.

#3087. Apollo to buy nearly 10% stake in Abu Dhabi-backed alternative asset manager Mubadala Capital

Investing giant Apollo Global Management is finalizing a deal to buy nearly a 10% stake in Mubadala Capital, the alternative asset manager subsidiary of Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, Mubadala Investment Co., according to people familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The deal is expected to be announced later Monday morning, they said. Financial terms were not immediately known.

The transaction is significant on multiple fronts. It further advances Apollo's ambitions in Abu Dhabi often called the "capital of capital." The firm has spent the past 15 years building key strategic relationships there, with both the country's investment arm and its core leadership.

Apollo already has a multibillion-dollar partnership with Mubadala Investment Co., first established in 2022 and extended two years ago. At the time of that extension, Apollo said the agreement would strengthen the firm's Capital Solutions platform by enabling the firms to jointly source and provide customized debt and equity financing to companies worldwide.

In 2023, the institutions formed a $2.5 billion joint venture designed specifically to co-invest in global private credit opportunities over a five-year horizon.

For Mubadala Capital specifically — the region's only large-scale asset manager, advising and administering more than $755 billion in assets — the deal further advances its growth strategy under the direction of CEO Hani Barhoush, and its relevance on the global investing stage. It also marks an inflection point for the company's core alternatives business, which has grown to more than $60 billion.

John Zito, co-president of Apollo's Asset Management arm, and Barhoush have worked closely together over the past several years and, according to sources, their close-knit relationship and the success of prior partnerships led to talks of deepening ties. So did the belief that scale in the asset management business matters more than ever.

"Capital as a moat is a big thing," said one person familiar with the deal.

Importantly, the deal also continues a notable shift in the relationship between American investment firms and the Middle East. While the region, and Abu Dhabi specifically, has long been a sought-after source of capital, this deal further reverses that dynamic, with Apollo making a significant direct investment in the country and its investment vision.

Mubadala Capital's international offices include London, New York, Rio de Janeiro and San Francisco.

Apollo's investment in Mubadala Capital is similar to deals the firm has done with other asset management platforms, including Diameter Capital, Thoreau, Motive Partners and others.

Spokespersons for both firms declined to comment.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates went up today, but they're still in a much better place than this time last month.

Mortgage rates are higher today, but only by a little. And they're still hovering below 7%, which is much better than what we saw around this time last month.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked up to 6.98% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is two basis points higher than Friday and five basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Mortgage rates have more room to rise, as a stronger-than-expected jobs report reinforced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

As for what’s next: Tomorrow’s jobs report, showing October data, could potentially nudge mortgage rates in either direction. To understand the link between jobs data and mortgage rates, keep reading below the video.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This week, the Nerds are watching the October Consumer Price Index, which comes out on Tuesday. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Right now, the labor market is looking pretty darn strong: The October jobs report, released Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, showed U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than economists expected, and unemployment edged down to 4.1%.

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, but rate hikes are only on the table when the labor market is strong enough to handle it. Considering Friday’s jobs data, it’s looking fairly likely that the Fed will approve a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Still, a jump in mortgage rates isn’t a sure thing, and market sentiment could shift over the next month. October’s inflation data will capture the effect of the Fed’s last rate hike, which came in the middle of September. If that worked as intended and inflation shows signs of slowing, mortgage rates might remain around 7%.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.48% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3085. Factorial Energy (FAC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Early aerospace deliveries arrived, but a $1.8 million inventory write-down hit gross results.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Factorial Energy Inc. (FAC -4.70%) transitioned to a commercial-stage company in the third quarter of 2026, recording its first revenue from solid-state battery cell deliveries to the aerospace market. Management reported reaching an energy density of 450 watt-hours per kilogram for its aerospace cells, meeting its year-end performance target ahead of schedule while achieving a pilot line yield of 85%. The company is executing a fabless business model, forming strategic partnerships with manufacturers like SK On to leverage existing global production capacity for the automotive sector. Factorial revised its full-year spending and capital expenditure guidance downward, citing cost reclassifications and disciplined operational management as it prepares for meaningful revenue growth in 2027.

And I think for our aerospace market, we are likely going to be focused more on the lithium metals technology to begin with because that is really the holy grail.

And in the automotive market, I think we see a combination of interest of both. So I would say, like, even between fast and solstice, there is interest for both like, silicon and lithium metal and other chemistries. And since we have not shared in more detail, it is roughly about half and half in terms of our customer interest at this moment.

Mark Schuster: that is very helpful. Thanks, Siyu. Just 1 more if I can fit it in. Just touching that last point, the demand for non-FEOC compliant sales, especially in the drone market, is high. And there is a timing component where a cell today is very important, and the performance of that cell may not even need to be off benchmark. it is just because the availability of supply is so low. I am wondering if there is a trade off or optimization of okay, I can make silicon cells faster and easier today, but, you know, they are not as good as performance of the lithium metal or annulus or solid state.

But customers prefer cells today versus waiting 2 years. Have you seen anything like that in your engagement? With, customers?

Siyu Huang: Mhmm. Mhmm. Yes. that is a great question. I think, actually, I do not see much difference between the time to market for the non-FEOC supply chain for either silicon or lithium metal. For us, specifically, because we have this. 1 of the strongest partnership coalition, with POSCO FUTURE M, which is 1 of the largest material maker in Korea, and they are also the only 1 producing both cathode and anode materials. And also a few other partners such as LG Chem over the years and even Sungeo High-tech on the recycling side. So I think we do have a really strong position in having access to 1 of the most advanced material supply chain. Globally.

And that is why. And we also have the. We have been focused on innovating products ourselves internally. So this gave us almost the same time in developing NDAA compliant cell for silicon versus for lithium metal. And I think I know what you are asking here is more for a lithium-metal supply chain. We do have a solution for that, and I will be able to share with you, hopefully, by the end of next quarter.

Mark Schuster: Great. Thank you very much.

Operator: Our next question is from Eric Goldstein with Water Tower Research. Please proceed with your question.

Eric Goldstein: Hey, good afternoon, guys, and congrats on all the accomplishments this quarter. I just had a couple of other questions. You put together a, you know, pretty impressive list of partners. I was just wondering how do you manage all the partners? Do you have employees that are colocated at their facilities? Are they colocated in your facilities? And where it makes sense, are you able to share advancements that are made with your partners across your entire ecosystem?

Siyu Huang: that is a great question, Eric. Thanks for dialing in today. Yes. So for. You know, our partnerships, especially with our customers and suppliers have been growing constantly over the course of last few years. With, you know, Mercedes de Lantus in early days and Hyundai-Kia and even with VW's recent onboarding. it is definitely really strong coalition together But I think we have had a very clear firewall on the technology and our trade secrets internally with our partners. And I think I would say all of our partners have been very respectful. For our technology too. So we have not really had have to have the partner to come in.

Of course, when it comes to say, automotive uptake, you will be a different You will have quality people getting to your room. That will be a different story. But I think at this stage and also with our drone customers, they are pretty hands off at this moment. And what we also realize that usually when you have big OEMs or drone customers sitting in a room before you receive uptake, that means that something's going wrong. So I think we. Fortunately, we do not have that issue. But I think we do have very close collaborations with our automotive partners.

We actually had multiple interviews and even co presentations in conferences, in press releases together, And I think a lot of people did not realize how closely the relationship is held it with each other. And, you know, from the earlier this year, we announced the 3 partners across 3 continents with KULR in the US, that is a NYSE publicly listed company for drone and aerospace integration with Tulip. As you know from the name, it is from Netherlands and JR from Korea. So those 3 companies across 3 continents.

And just over the course of last few months with the world record, and we set with the Game of Drones event and even with partners with the LIFT challenge and all these different competitions. And those partners have helped a lot in this process. So we sometimes, do visit their facility. And they also visit us. But I think it is a very friendly conversation, and then we also keep a little bit healthy distance with each other.

Eric Goldstein: Okay. Great. Just a couple others. The SKON, m u. MOU? Are there any milestones to that would turn that into a definitive agreement?

Siyu Huang: Yes. We actually have a lot of milestones within MOU. Apparently, like, we do not have authority to disclose it as of today.

Siyu Huang: But I would say just from my perspective, from the company's perspective, our next big milestone is really the uptake from OEM. I think that is really the 1 that we are looking into to build beyond those nitty gritty small detailed milestones that we signed in an MOU. I think that is gonna be a big driver to bring everything together.

Eric Goldstein: Okay. And then just 1 for Richard. It looks like the cash burn in the third quarter was a little higher than what it had been in the first half of the year. I am just wondering how you are thinking about the fourth quarter Do you expect cash usage in the fourth quarter to be similar to the third quarter?

C. Wei: I provided guidance for the full year. About 36 to 38 range. that is on a non GAAP basis. I think you could deduce what the Q4 number should be based on that. We will continue to do inventory.

Eric Goldstein: Okay. And then just the last 1, the $4 million legal judgment, was that paid out in the third quarter?

C. Wei: That was paid out in the fourth quarter.

#3084. Best Hotels in Chase’s The Edit in 2026

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website.
