With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Chase's hotel and resort program, The Edit, gives some cardholders the chance to book stays at spectacular hotels.

Many premium credit cards have their own travel portals where you can earn and redeem your points. They also have a curated list of hotels with which they partner to offer elevated benefits to their cardholders who book directly through their program.

The Edit is Chase’s program, and similar to the Fine Hotels & Resorts program from American Express, travelers need to book a prepaid reservation directly through a Chase Travel channel and pay with their Chase card to receive the benefits.

What benefits do you receive when you book through the program? Well, they can be substantial.

At nearly 1,400 hotels and resorts, The Edit customers will enjoy:

If the hotel is an all-inclusive property, guests would instead receive a $200 property credit to use for experiences like spa treatments. While stays at hotels in The Edit Boutique Collection do include the other perks, those stays are not eligible for a room upgrade or early check-in/late checkout considerations.

The tradeoff of using The Edit program is that it does not necessarily always have the lowest rate. Sometimes you can find a lower rate directly with the hotel or another website. But, when you consider the list of benefits above, any differential in price can more than outweigh the extra cost.

While it belongs to Chase, The Edit is not open to all Chase cardholders. It is a dedicated perk for primary cardholders and authorized users of the Chase Sapphire Reserve® and J.P. Morgan Reserve cards, as well as primary Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ cardholders.

Even better is that these eligible Chase cards come with a total of $500 in credits that can be used at The Edit hotels each year. They are divided into two $250 credits that each must be used for at least a two-night stay. And when paying for the rest of your stay through The Edit, cardholders earn 8x Chase Ultimate Rewards® points per dollar spent. In addition, hotel stays booked through The Edit and labeled as “Loyalty Plus” are eligible to also earn points with any associated hotel loyalty program.

These are some of our favorite hotels in the program where you can take advantage of your annual $500 credits as well as earn significant Chase points for a prepaid stay.

This oasis in the desert enjoys distant views of the Atlas Mountains from its various pools and riad-like accommodation buildings. It also has a full-service spa, kids club and access to Al Maaden Golf course. Its Moroccan restaurant is worth a visit and offers cuisine from all of Morocco and the North African region (with many ingredients coming from the chef’s onsite garden). Guests can add a stash of World of Hyatt points to their account after a stay here, but be sure to look to see if it is “eligible” in the search results (as shown below).

Guests can arrive at this luxury resort by its own fleet of two sea planes that serve the three properties in the Four Seasons portfolio. (Two of the properties are in The Edit, the third is a private island: Four Seasons Maldives Kuda Huraa, Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Landaa Giraavaru and Four Seasons Maldives Private Island at Voavah, respectively.)

Overwater villas with their own pools and hammocks dangling over the sea, beach bungalows with private access pools and excellent dining (from Asian to Lebanese) are hallmarks of the resort. Its newest element is the AyurMa wellness program at the spa with onsite practitioners who guide guests on personalized, multiday journeys covering everything from nutrition to physical therapy.

This resort is designed around 64 pool suites and villas with access to a beautiful beachfront, swimming pools and a jungle spa. Its island location lies within the Gulf of Thailand near Koh Samui, and its beach is well-known for its famous Full Moon parties. Other activities, besides relaxing, include Muay Thai boxing, scuba diving, snorkeling, kayaking, stand-up paddle boarding and yoga sessions.

Anantara is part of Minor Hotels that are associated with the Discovery program, which means travelers can earn Discovery Dollars, even when booking via The Edit.

Along the Southbank Promenade, this luxury hotel has great views of the Melbourne skyline and is within walking distance of the city’s great shopping, museums and dining options. When you enter the lobby, the first thing you notice is the grand Waterford crystal chandelier, one of the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.

This is also one of the city’s biggest hotels, and it is highly regarded as a top hotel in town. Be sure to request one of the rooms with a balcony or terrace to take in the views.

Known by many as Dublin’s grande dame, this Autograph Collection member is fresh off the heels of a top-to-bottom renovation that renewed its interiors, but didn’t change its historic spirit. While renovation work will linger into 2027, the refreshed rooms are worth experiencing.

The hotel is where the drafting of the Irish Constitution took place, but today it serves as a hub for visiting elite and locals to mix and mingle. When booking through The Edit, members can earn Marriott Bonvoy points in addition to Chase Ultimate Rewards®.

This beachfront hotel is a favorite destination for European travelers who want a Dalmatian coastline view while also being in close proximity to the historic center of town. There are multiple pools, a beach club and spa for onsite entertainment. Radisson Rewards members would also be able to earn points for their stay.

Radisson is growing its portfolio of high-end hotels, resorts and luxury properties, which makes the loyalty program one not to overlook for Americans who may not be as familiar with it.

This city-center hotel is ideal for business travelers, but also attracts attention for its rooftop bar and restaurant. Chase cardholders using The Edit should think beyond just booking a vacation stay through the program because business trips can also yield significant Ultimate Rewards points bonuses. Just remember you need to book through The Edit with a prepaid, eligible rate.

In a historic bank building, the hotel’s Bauhaus-inspired design with colorful art make this more than just a standard business property. And like Kimpton properties worldwide, guests here can take advantage of morning coffee and refreshments in the lobby, an evening happy hour, free bikes and yoga mats to use, and of course the secret password. Mention that password (which changes seasonally) at reception to be eligible for a prize that could include drink vouchers or room upgrades among other things.

This family-friendly resort features the largest and first waterpark on the island (with three waterslides and a lazy river) as well as some of its finest dining venues, including the only high-end steakhouse on the island. Golfers can enjoy the island’s only 18-hole golf course here, too.

Because it's an independent resort, booking through The Edit is a great way to still earn points for your stay since it does not have a loyalty program of its own.

Celebrating 100 years, the hotel has unveiled renovations across the hotel, which sits in midtown Manhattan, and they will continue for the next year. Guests who book a Club rate or have the annual lounge benefit they can select as a Milestone Reward can visit the lobby-level club lounge here.

The building was built as part of the Grand Central Terminal design plan and now belongs to the Historic Hotels of America group. Guests who book through The Edit will receive IHG One Rewards for their stay and any eligible elite status perks.

The “Pink Palace of the Pacific” will celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2027 and is a famous hotel along one of Hawaii’s most famous beaches. This is one of many Marriott Bonvoy family hotels in Honolulu, and it is surrounded by lush gardens and has stunning ocean views. Guests can walk to nearby shopping, take the onsite history tour or snap photos with Diamond Head in the background. Guests can earn Marriott Bonvoy points for their stay, and elite status members can take advantage of any eligible perks.

This all-inclusive, family hotel is a great option for those looking for great dining, sunshine and oceanfront accommodations. Parents can enjoy the spa while kids are having fun in the kids club. Other activities include movie nights outside, painting classes, beach barbecues and lawn games. The resort is part of the Preferred Hotels & Resorts program, and earning Ultimate Rewards points for booking a stay through The Edit is a nice bonus.

Prepare for a new experience at one of the Chilean capital’s most posh hotels, and you can book your entire stay through The Edit. As a result, you would receive the perks of the program as well as Marriott Bonvoy points at the only Ritz-Carlton in South America.

Big changes at the hotel include new menus that refocus the restaurant cuisine on modern takes of Chilean recipes. The chef partners with a local farmer for produce, but goes one step further in being able to have first dibs on the best produce and herbs available each season. On the top floor, guests can enjoy a panoramic indoor swimming pool beneath a glass atrium, panoramic rooftop terrace and spa offering traditional Andean healing treatments.

Booking a hotel via The Edit leads to instant benefits like free breakfast, property credits, and early check-in and late checkout. While the rates may not always be the lowest you’ll find online, the perks that come with The Edit may more than outweigh any cost differential.

The Edit’s curated collection of hotels and resorts covers a broad range of high-end properties, and the program is only open to select Chase credit cardholders. When making a prepaid, eligible reservation through The Edit, the cardholder also receives 8x Ultimate Rewards points on top of the onsite perks that make this a great offer. Even better, if the property participates in its own loyalty program, Chase has worked out that members can double dip and earn Chase Ultimate Rewards® and the relevant hotel points and potential elite status perks, too (as long as it is labeled as “eligible” in the search function).

Don’t forget about the $500 in built-in credits that come with your card, which renew each year and only further the value with Chase’s The Edit program.

#3083. Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income

Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

"While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the company to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

"As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent announced an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

"CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," said Richardson.

The 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.

Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

#3081. The Homebuying Advice Service Members Need (but Don’t Always Get)

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

VA mortgage borrowers are quietly navigating a knowledge gap. Here’s how to close it.

If your understanding of a VA home loan starts and ends with “it’s for the military,” you’re not alone. For many eligible veterans and service members, the intricate workings (and benefits) of this U.S. government-backed mortgage are obscured behind lackluster guidance.

While there are classes and resources available, the military is broadly wary of steering members in a specific direction, says Alex Rodino, a real estate agent and U.S. Army veteran who served 10 years as an infantry officer and military advisor. “A lot of the course material is just very generic,” he says.

And that’s not a surprise. Considering the sheer size and scope of the military, providing personalized advice on VA loans to all its members would be no easy task.

That leaves real estate agents and lenders as the last line of defense, which is where a big part of the knowledge gap exists. Rodino purchased his first home in 2020 with a VA loan and says he didn’t like how ignorant he felt during the process.

“The reason I actually got my real estate license to begin with was because of that experience I had,” Rodino says. “Looking back on it, I had a lot of questions that didn't really get answered.”

But how can VA borrowers navigate this knowledge gap without having to become mortgage experts in their spare time? Here are some of the most important things to know when considering a VA loan, according to the financial experts and borrowers who have lived it.

“My mortgage broker said, hey, you might qualify for this, look it up,” says Elizabeth Valente, a real estate investor and former U.S. Army officer who bought her first home using a VA loan in 2021. When it came to the application process, she felt crucial information wasn’t readily available to her or fully explained.

In hindsight, Valente says, working with an agent or lender who had detailed VA loan experience would have been beneficial. Not only would it help untangle the specific paperwork and appraisal requirements, but that expertise offers an important layer of support for military borrowers.

“For some processes in the military, it's very hand-holding,” Valente says. “I'll tell you what to wear, what to bring, when to be there.” But that’s not always true when transitioning back to civilian life, and parsing specifics of a loan process can be challenging. “I don't think a typical Realtor would understand what that person's going through,” Valente says.

Finding professionals with the right expertise involves asking questions — and lots of them.

“If I'm the smartest person in the room, we have an issue,” Valente says. “Don't be afraid to tell someone if something doesn't make sense or if you don't understand the numbers.”

Before agreeing to work with a lender or mortgage broker, ask how their process works, what companies they work with, and how familiar they are with VA loans. Treat the initial conversation like an interview — you’re hiring them, not the other way around.

Knowing where to find your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) and how much you might be eligible to borrow is the responsibility of the person applying, Valente says. “All that information — it is available in the [VA] website but you really have to dig for it.”

And this information isn’t recreational reading — your COE lists your "basic entitlement," which is a crucial figure in VA lending. If you have full basic entitlement, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) generally guarantees 25% of the loan, which in most cases lets you put 0% down.

Why? With a quarter of the loan guaranteed by the VA, the lender is more protected and thus more willing to forgo a down payment.

So how do you know if you have full basic entitlement? Look for the figure $36,000 on your COE. This dollar amount represents full entitlement. Technically, basic entitlement is for loans up to $144,000, but then your bonus entitlement kicks in and you can go higher. The VA doesn’t set loan limits when you have full entitlement — though your lender will still decide how much you can borrow based on your income, debts, credit and the home’s appraised value.

Let’s say you want to buy a home in Fayetteville, North Carolina, and you need a $200,000 loan. In order to put no money down, your entitlement needs to cover at least 25% of the loan amount — in this example, that’s $50,000. After you purchase the home, your COE will show your basic entitlement as $0 and the entitlement charged to a previous loan as $50,000.

“Serving in the military is a unique investing opportunity that most people don't get,” Rodino says. “I wish someone had told me to buy a house when I got to my first duty station.”

If he’d known it was possible or understood how, Rodino says he would have been able to buy in 2017, move in 2020, rent out his first home and then repeat the process. “I'd have three by now and the first one would probably be paid off.”

This particular plan is partly based on the unique schedule of many military members. “Generally, you're moving anywhere from two to four to six years,” Rodino says. Owning multiple properties also leverages two big (and often misunderstood) perks of the VA loan: It’s possible to have more than one active loan at the same time, and after one year, you may be able to convert your primary residence to a rental.

Let’s go back to Fayetteville, North Carolina. After two years, you decide to rent out the home because you’re moving to Bell County, Texas. The home you want to buy in Bell County is $300,000, and in order to make no down payment, you need the VA to guarantee 25% of the loan ($75,000).

Because you no longer have full basic entitlement — remember, you already have an active VA loan elsewhere — your entitlement is capped at 25% of the conforming loan limit in the county where you plan to buy, minus what’s already being used on your first loan ($50,000 in our Fayetteville example).

Now for the math: The current conforming loan limit in Bell County is $832,750. Multiply this figure by 25% and subtract the $50,000 already in use: You have $158,187.50 of entitlement available to you — plenty to guarantee the $75,000 needed on the new loan.

If all of this sounds overwhelming, you’re not wrong. There are resources out there to help you figure all of this out, Rodino says. “The problem is, they're not always practical or they're not always apparent.”

The VA has a website that can walk you through entitlement calculations, but you should also ask your lender, broker or agent. If you’re working with experienced folks, they’ll be able to explain these details and help you get the most out of the VA’s guarantees.

The key takeaway is this: While each VA loan must initially be for a primary residence, borrowers can leverage their entitlement to build an investment portfolio without needing to cough up large down payments.

But these examples don’t consider all of the factors that go into approvals. Like most mortgages, your income, debts and assets dictate your eligibility. And although the VA doesn’t impose credit score minimums, most lenders do — NerdWallet's analysis shows 620 is a common floor.

It’s also important to note that a VA loan’s 0% down isn’t free. VA loans carry a funding fee based on how much you’re putting down and whether it’s your first or subsequent use (certain disabled veterans are exempt). You can pay this up front at closing or roll it into the loan amount; again, your team of professionals should be able to walk you through your options.

“I think there's the assumption that this is what we do: We get our VA home loan and we go buy a home,” says Julie Soares, financial readiness director for the Wounded Warrior Project. When we’re given access to a benefit that offers discounts and perks, it can be hard not to take advantage of it. But this is why financial awareness is critical.

There are a lot of conversations happening right now around homeownership and whether it’s the right choice, especially as affordability remains challenging. So if you haven’t heard it recently, here’s a reminder: Buying property is not the only way to build wealth or create financial security.

“The financial readiness program at Wounded Warrior Project is really leaning into getting further upstream in those conversations,” Soares says. Having a clear understanding of your benefits before you need to use them allows you to make more informed choices.

While it's helpful to understand your entitlement and what you may be eligible to borrow, you don't have to know every little detail about mortgages, or navigate the process alone. Sometimes, the most important thing to know about VA loans is where to turn for help.

If you are unsure of your eligibility or want more information about home loans, you can call the VA's home loans hotline at 877-827-3702.

“Please reach out to Wounded Warrior Project, reach out to the VA, reach out to any service organization,” Soares says. “Not one organization is gonna be able to fix or solve all of these problems. We have to do this as a group.”

#3079. Rocket Lab: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Electron's 96% mission success rate across nearly 100 flights gives customers a track record to lean on before committing to Neutron's premium pricing.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 9, 2026, Rocket Lab (RKLB +6.54%) reported quarterly revenue of $268 million, representing 73% year-over-year growth. Global launch supply remains constrained, so spacecraft builders with proven flight hardware can command higher prices. Scaling flight cadence and software capabilities expands the company's addressable market. Three key takeaways from management stand out for long-term investors.

Global launch availability remains tight, so rocket providers can raise launch fees rather than offer early customer discounts. For Neutron, its new medium-lift launch vehicle designed to carry 13 tonnes, customer demand pushed base contract prices higher as early flight slots filled up into the next decade.

Execution consistency matters for satellite operators who can't afford payload delays. Rocket Lab manufactures the Electron, its small orbital launch vehicle, at a rapid pace while maintaining a 96% mission success rate across nearly 100 flights, helping it retain commercial and defense customers.

Expanding beyond launch into constellation management provides predictable recurring revenue. Rocket Lab completed a $2.4 billion at-the-market equity offering program, in which it sells shares in the open market over time.

Launch capacity constraints and satellite constellation build-outs continue to surge, driving factory floors to full operational capacity. In its Space Systems segment, which designs and builds satellites and components, Rocket Lab maintains an operational footprint spanning solar cells, flight software, and satellite subassemblies. Vertically integrated manufacturing shields the company from broader supply chain bottlenecks. Meanwhile, growing backlog, which represents signed customer contracts awaiting delivery, provides long-term revenue visibility while management focuses on launch cadence execution and cost discipline.

Building reusable rocket infrastructure requires substantial early capital investments, but established operational momentum positions the company to capture expanding market share across commercial and national security missions.

#3069. TransDigm: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Its decentralized bolt-on model lets TransDigm grow without betting the company on oversized deals.

On its fourth quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, TransDigm (TDG +0.55%) announced fiscal 2027 revenue guidance with a midpoint of $12.05 billion. That top-line target reflects double-digit expansion across key aerospace markets, offering long-term investors a clear look at how disciplined capital deployment drives earnings. Three things management said stand out.

TransDigm relies on its 57 operating units to identify and integrate small acquisitions, known as bolt-ons, rather than depending solely on central dealmakers. This decentralized approach expands the acquisition pipeline without forcing the company into risky, oversized deals.

Temporary dips in passenger travel don't crush demand for replacement parts because airlines must keep existing fleets operational. TransDigm expects commercial aftermarket revenue to recover to baseline levels whenever short-term travel disruptions end.

New military repair regulations pose little threat because TransDigm self-funds product development and holds proprietary intellectual property (IP) rights. Direct sales to the government account for roughly 6% of revenue, and less than 1% involves repairable parts.

Factory automation drives margin expansion as original equipment manufacturer (OEM) production climbs. TransDigm focuses capital expenditures (capex) on efficiency gains while tracking factory productivity to preserve operational leverage.

Proprietary aerospace parts provide structural moats that generate durable cash flow. Management monitors capital allocation opportunities and maintains substantial liquidity to deploy when attractive acquisitions emerge.

#3068. Investors are doing just as well this year by shunning AI. How to invest if the tech trade keeps fizzling

A version of the S&P 500 without AI briefly pulled ahead of the traditional index this year and is now neck-and-neck as investors rotate into other areas of the market.

A proprietary Goldman Sachs index tracking the S&P 500 without stocks classified as "AI enablers" was up 12.4% through Oct. 22, edging ahead of the standard S&P 500's 12% gain. The Goldman index is now neck-and-neck with the S&P 500 as tech rallied in Monday trading.

Tech and AI-related companies make up about 45% of the S&P 500. That heavy weighting has helped power the index for years, but it's turned into a liability lately; the S&P 500 tech sector is down about 7% this month while other sectors have held up.

Investors have soured on debt and equity issued by companies like CoreWeave and Oracle. Shares of Meta Platforms sank almost 7% Thursday after it outlined more plans to spend heavily on capex and issue additional shares.

Companies supplying power and equipment for the buildout have been hit hard — names like GE Vernova, Bloom Energy, Vistra and Quanta Services all suffered steep declines during the recent selloff.

Goldman, which launched the measure earlier this year with S&P, uses the S&P 500 as its starting universe and excludes companies perceived to be enablers of AI before applying S&P 500 Index weighting methodology to the remaining universe of companies.

The ex-AI index lagged the S&P 500 for most of the year as investors continued to favor chipmakers, cloud-computing companies and other firms benefiting from heavy AI spending. However, that advantage has been narrowing and it disappeared last week.

Meanwhile, investors are rotating into defensive areas. ETFs like State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF, State Street Health Select SPDR ETF and State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF are up 7% to 10% this month. Energy is ahead 10% too, though that's more related to the war in Iran.

Some analysts recommend sticking with non-AI companies for diversification and protection against more pain in tech. The "AI pendulum has swung back in favor of non-AI exposure over the last two weeks," Oppenheimer technical analyst Ari Wald said in a note on Oct. 24.

Two industries that Oppenheimer favors now are commercial services and insurance. The firm upgraded those industries to overweight last week, recommending Republic Services, Cintas, Verisk Analytics, Broadridge Financial Solutions, MetLife and Arthur J. Gallagher.

Berkshire Hathaway is also capitalizing on the rotation out of tech. Its Class B shares are up 8% this month, though it's still lagging behind the S&P 500 this year.

Berkshire owns a wide swath of operating companies, including insurance giant Geico and Burlington Northern Santa Fe railroad. It also has a $364 billion stock portfolio including companies like Apple, Coca-Cola, Alphabet and Bank of America. That diversification may help Berkshire continue to outperform if the tech sector drags down the S&P 500.

Trivector Research sees potential in "non-tech compounders." Healthcare giant Eli Lilly is one idea. The stock is up 22% on the strength of Lilly's weight-loss drugs. The company has more in the pipeline, including a next-generation obesity drug that Lilly plans to file for FDA approval early in 2027.

Viking Holdings, a cruise operator, is also proving durable. The company said on its August earnings call that 40% of its river capacity and 60% of its ocean capacity was already booked for 2027. "Based on recent events, we've seen our guests have proved to be resilient and are continuing to book 2027 and future seasons," the company told investors.

Viking stock is up 15% this year but it may still have upside. The average Wall Street target is $109, above recent prices around $82. Barclays recently upgraded the cruise operator to overweight with a $102 target, citing the company's "compelling risk/reward."

#3067. First Look: Inside United’s New Club at Washington Dulles

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.
